## Important Tips

- Compare minimum deposit requirements (often $200-$300)
- Check if the issuer does automatic reviews for upgrading

# Secured Credit Cards for Rebuilding Credit

Here are solid options to consider, along with what to look for:

## Top Picks

**Discover it® Secured**
- Deposit: $200 minimum
- Notable: Cashback rewards (rare for secured cards), matches your first year of cash back
- Discover reviews accounts starting around month 8 for graduation to unsecured

**Capital One Platinum Secured**
- Deposit: As low as $49, $99, or $200 depending on creditworthiness (sometimes less than your credit limit)
- Notable: Automatic reviews for credit line increases and graduation after responsible use

**Citi® Secured Mastercard**
- Deposit: $200 minimum
- Notable: Reports to all three bureaus, straightforward terms

## What Actually Matters for Your Goals

**1. Low minimum deposit** — since funds are tight, prioritize cards with $200 or less minimums (or ones like Capital One that scale based on your situation)

**2. Automatic graduation path** — Discover and Capital One both have track records of reviewing accounts for upgrade to unsecured without you needing to apply separately or get your deposit locked up in a new application

**3. No/low annual fee** — avoid cards that charge $35-50/year; many secured cards have $0 fees

**4. Reports to all 3 bureaus** — confirm this before applying (most major ones do, but double-check)

## Your 12-Month Game Plan

- **Keep utilization under 30%**, ideally under 10% (e.g., if limit is $200, keep balance under $20)
- **Set up autopay** for at least the minimum to avoid any new missed payments
- **Don't apply for multiple cards at once** — one hard inquiry is fine, but spread out other applications
- **Check for graduation eligibility** around month 6-7, even if the issuer doesn't auto-reach out

One more thing: your existing missed payments will still show on your report for up to 7 years, but new consistent on-time payments matter more and more as time passes. The secured card is really about demonstrating *new* responsible behavior.

prompt: We're a couple, one of us is vegetarian, we have about 30 minutes to cook on weeknights and want to stay around $12 a serving. Recommend meal kit delivery services.
text:
Based on current 2026 reviews, here are meal kit services that fit your needs well — feeding two, with solid vegetarian menus, ~30-minute recipes, and prices that land at or under your $12/serving target.

## Top Picks

**HelloFresh** – The best all-around fit. HelloFresh is the world's largest meal kit for a reason, hitting the sweet spot of price, variety, and quality, priced around $7.49-$10.99/serving. It also has a vegetarian menu option alongside its broader catalog, with pricing around $11.99 per serving for vegetarian-specific recipes. With 30+ weekly recipes, you'll easily find 20-30 minute options and plenty of veggie-forward dishes your vegetarian partner can pick from each week.

**Home Chef** – Best value + biggest vegetarian selection. It has more than 270 vegetarian options in the catalog, and the lowest starting price per serving on this list for dinners, starting at $6.99 per serving. Home Chef is well known for clearly labeled quick-cook options, so it's easy to filter for 30-minutes-or-less recipes while staying well under $12/serving even after the intro discount expires.

**Blue Apron** – Good quality-to-price ratio with flexibility. Blue Apron's cost per serving ranges from $9.49 to $14.99, with shipping at $9.99 (or free with Blue Apron+ membership), 2 or 4 servings per meal, and it's noted as vegetarian-friendly. Recently in 2026, Blue Apron introduced a more flexible ordering model, allowing customers to purchase meals without a subscription, so you can order à la carte and pick only quick vegetarian-friendly recipes as needed — handy for staying near $12/serving without being locked into a weekly plan.

**Sunbasket** – Great if you want more premium/organic ingredients but still want to hit budget. Sunbasket starts at $12 per serving for meal kits (and $10 for its Fresh & Ready prepared meals), with an additional $6 for shipping, offering 2 or 4 servings and 2 to 5 meals per week. It lands right at your $12 ceiling, so it's worth it mainly if you value organic produce and don't mind being right at the edge of budget.

## Honorable Mention (if you want dedicated vegetarian/vegan variety)

**Green Chef** – If the vegetarian partner wants a wider plant-based rotation and you don't mind paying slightly more some weeks, Green Chef offers a dedicated plan with three to eight recipes per week for two, four or six people, and is vegetarian friendly. However, pricing runs starting from $13.99 per serving plus $10.99 shipping, which can push you over $12/serving unless you catch a promo — so treat it as an occasional splurge rather than your everyday pick.

## Bottom line for your situation
Given you're a couple with one vegetarian, 30-minute cook time, and a ~$12/serving ceiling, I'd start with **HelloFresh or Home Chef** — both have large, clearly labeled vegetarian menus, abundant quick-prep recipes, and per-serving pricing that comfortably sits at or below your budget once you filter out the premium/specialty recipes. Blue Apron's new no-subscription model is also worth trying if you want more control over picking only the fastest, cheapest vegetarian options week to week.

Secured credit cards are a great tool for building or rebuilding credit since they require a refundable cash deposit (which typically becomes your credit limit) and report your payment activity to the major credit bureaus. Here are some of the top options across different needs:

### 🏆 Best Overall / Low Deposit
**Capital One Platinum Secured Credit Card** – with this card, you may qualify for an opening credit line of at least $200 with a refundable deposit starting at $49. The annual fee is $0. It's also noted that it is one of the few secured credit cards that may extend you a credit line that is greater than your security deposit.

### 💰 Best for Rewards
**Capital One Quicksilver Secured Cash Rewards Credit Card** – Offers flat-rate cash back with no annual fee; the Quicksilver Secured card earns unlimited 1.5% cash back on all purchases and has no annual fee.

**Discover it® Secured Credit Card** – it earned the title of "best card for building credit" in the NerdWallet Best-Of Awards every year from 2018 to 2026, and it has a $0 annual fee.

**Bank of America® Unlimited Cash Rewards Secured Credit Card** – offers 1.5% cash back on all purchases and has a $0 annual fee.

### 📈 Best for High Credit Limit
**BankAmericard® Secured Credit Card** – offers the potential for an exceptionally high credit limit for a secured card — up to $5,000.

**Platinum Secured Mastercard® from First Tech Federal Credit Union** – has a maximum credit limit of $25,000. It also features a fairly low variable APR range.

### 🚫 Best for No Credit Check
**OpenSky® Plus Secured Visa® Credit Card** – there's no annual fee, no credit check and no minimum required security deposit upfront.

### 💳 Best Low-Fee / Low-Interest Option
**DCU Visa® Platinum Secured Credit Card** – it's the rare secured card that charges minimal fees (no annual fee, no foreign transaction fee, no cash advance fee, no balance transfer fee) and doesn't default to charging the highest possible interest rate (its APRs as of 2026 range from 15% to 18%).

**Navy Federal cashRewards Secured Credit Card** (requires NFCU membership) – no annual fee, no foreign transaction fees, a notably low 18.00% APR compared to the 25-29% range most secured cards charge, and unlimited 1% cash back on every purchase.

### 📊 Best for Tracking Credit Score
**Citi® Secured Mastercard®** – it's a no annual fee credit card that helps you build your credit when used responsibly, with free monthly FICO® credit score access and reports monthly to all three major credit bureaus.

### 🏦 Best Flexible Deposit
**Secured Chime Visa® Credit Card** – the money you move into the secured account is the amount you can spend on your card (no minimum deposit required!). Turn on Safer Credit Building and have your monthly balance automatically paid on time.

---

### What to Consider When Choosing
- **Annual fee**: Many top cards (Capital One Platinum/Quicksilver, Discover it Secured, Citi Secured, DCU, Chime) charge **$0**.
- **Deposit flexibility**: Some allow deposits as low as $49, while others require $200+ upfront.
- **Graduation path**: Look for issuers like Capital One, which reviews your account for graduation as early as 6 months, letting you eventually get your deposit back and move to an unsecured card.
- **Rewards**: If you want cash back while building credit, Discover it Secured, Capital One Quicksilver Secured, and BofA Unlimited Cash Rewards Secured are strong picks.

text:
# Secured Credit Cards for Rebuilding Credit

Here are solid options for your situation, with a focus on low deposits and fast graduation to unsecured cards:

## Top Picks

**Discover it® Secured Credit Card**
- Minimum deposit: $200
- Cashback rewards (2% at gas/restaurants, 1% everything else) — unusual for secured cards
- Discover reviews accounts starting around month 7-8 for graduation to unsecured
- No annual fee
- Reports to all 3 bureaus

**Capital One Platinum Secured Card**
- Minimum deposit can be as low as $49-$99-$200 depending on your credit (determined by a soft pull during application)
- Credit limit of $200+ even with smaller deposit (they sometimes match more than you put down)
- Automatic reviews for graduation, often within 6 months
- No annual fee

**Citi® Secured Mastercard®**
- $200 minimum deposit
- No annual fee
- Reports to all 3 bureaus
- Less flashy but reliable track record for graduation

## What Matters Most for Your Goal

1. **Confirm automatic graduation review** — Discover and Capital One both do periodic reviews without you needing to call and ask
2. **Low utilization** — Keep balance under 30% (ideally under 10%) of your limit each month
3. **On-time payments** — This is non-negotiable given your history; consider autopay for at least the minimum
4. **Don't close it early** — Even after graduating to unsecured products, length of history matters

## A Few Tactical Tips

- **Set up autopay for at least minimum payment** immediately — missed payments are what got you here, so remove human error from the equation
- **Ask about deposit matching** — Some issuers (like Capital One) extend credit lines beyond your deposit based on income
- **Avoid closing old negative accounts** — this doesn't help and can sometimes hurt if it reduces your average account age
- **Check your specific card's graduation policy** before applying — call customer service or check the account agreement, since policies can change

Given your 1-year timeline and missed payment history, Discover it Secured is probably your strongest option — the cashback is a nice bonus, but the automatic graduation review process is the real draw.

Here's a rundown of the top meal kit delivery services based on recent 2026 testing and reviews, organized by what you're looking for:

## Best Overall
**Blue Apron** and **HelloFresh** are the two names that consistently top "best overall" lists. Blue Apron is a meal kit pioneer, and nearly 15 years after launching, it's still rated as the best and most delicious service tested. Meanwhile, HelloFresh is frequently picked as the best meal kit delivery service thanks to its versatile and tasty recipes. It delivers big flavor and consistently excellent recipes with fresh ingredients, with enough variety to satisfy most diets.

## Best for Budget Shoppers
**EveryPlate** and **Dinnerly** are the go-to cheap options. EveryPlate is the budget meal kit service — one tester called it "by far the cheapest meal kit subscription" they'd tried. For an even more affordable option, Dinnerly delivers tasty, fuss-free meal kits starting at just $4.99 per serving.

## Best for Families
HelloFresh is frequently rated best for feeding the whole family, while Home Chef is a strong pick for vegetarian-friendly families because of the variety offered.

## Best for Variety / Picky Eaters
**Home Chef** stands out here. It's rated best if you're craving variety, and it stands out in any meal-kit comparison for its flexibility, offering both weekly meal kits and an Oven-Ready line for minimal prep.

## Best for Plant-Based/Vegan Diets
**Purple Carrot** is the top pick. It's rated best for vegans among the major services.

## Best for Convenience/Minimal Prep
**Tovala** and **Gobble** shine here if you're short on time. Tovala is noted as best for busy cooks, while Gobble offers pre-prepped kits for even faster cooking.

## Best Hybrid (Grocery + Meal Kit)
**Hungryroot** is unique in blending grocery delivery with recipes. It's a solid option if you're looking to skip trips to the grocery store altogether, and it blends the flexibility of an online grocery store with the convenience of a customizable meal kit while prioritizing clean, mostly organic ingredients.

## Pricing Overview
In general, price is one detail that should not be overlooked since you'll pay weekly or monthly, and meal kit delivery services tend to cost about $7 to $13 per serving, with some dishes going significantly higher for premium meals. Most services also charge shipping fees on top of that, though some (like Blue Apron) waive it with a membership.

---

### Quick Recommendation Summary
| Need | Best Pick |
|---|---|
| Overall quality | Blue Apron or HelloFresh |
| Tightest budget | EveryPlate or Dinnerly |
| Big families | HelloFresh |
| Variety/flexibility | Home Chef |
| Vegan/plant-based | Purple Carrot |
| Minimal effort | Tovala or Gobble |
| Grocery + recipes combo | Hungryroot |

Since most services offer a discounted first box, it's worth trying 2-3 that match your priorities to see which recipes and delivery experience you like best before committing to a subscription.

prompt: I live in New York and I'm new to crypto. I want to buy small amounts of bitcoin and ether every month, keep fees low and keep things simple. Recommend cryptocurrency exchange platforms.
text:
Since you're in New York, your options are narrower than the rest of the country — NY requires exchanges to hold a **BitLicense** or a New York trust charter from the NYDFS, which rules out some popular platforms like Kraken, Crypto.com, Binance.US, and KuCoin. Licensed exchanges available to New York residents include Coinbase, Gemini, Robinhood, eToro, and Bitstamp. Kraken, Crypto.com, Binance.US, and KuCoin are not available in New York.

For your specific goal — small monthly BTC/ETH buys, low fees, simplicity — here are the best picks:

## Top recommendations

**1. Coinbase (best all-around for beginners)**
Coinbase New York users benefit from full compliance with NYDFS regulations, which means tighter consumer protections and transparent operating standards. Coinbase offers its full suite of trading features, including wallet transfers, recurring buys, and tax documentation. One tip: the simple "buy" button on the main app charges higher fees than switching to **Coinbase Advanced Trade**, which uses a much lower maker/taker fee schedule — worth doing once you're comfortable.

**2. Gemini (NY-born, built for compliance)**
Gemini was founded in New York and is one of the only exchanges available in all 50 states. It's especially good for recurring buys: recurring purchases lose the trading fee after their first week, leaving only the spread. That makes it genuinely cheap for a "set it and forget it" monthly DCA strategy.

**3. Robinhood (simplest, commission-free)**
Robinhood is a BitLicense-registered crypto exchange legally operating in New York, meaning it meets all NYDFS regulatory requirements for offering crypto trading in the state. For New York residents, Robinhood allows you to buy and sell cryptocurrencies commission-free, which is great if you're just getting started or want simple exposure to crypto prices. If you mainly want to buy and hold BTC/ETH without needing advanced features (and don't need to move crypto to an external wallet often), this is about as simple and cheap as it gets.

**4. Strike (if you want a Bitcoin-focused, low-fee recurring buyer)**
Strike received its BitLicense in 2026, with bill pay and loans also cleared for New York. Deposit minimums are low, and dollar withdrawals are free. It's built around recurring purchases and is one of the newer, lower-cost options specifically for NY residents, though its focus is mainly Bitcoin rather than a wide range of assets.

**5. eToro (newly available, good multi-asset app)**
eToro switched on New York crypto trading in April 2026, giving NY residents another simple, well-designed mobile option if you ever want to diversify beyond BTC/ETH later.

## Practical tips to keep fees low on small monthly buys
- **Fund via bank transfer (ACH), not debit/credit card.** Card funding typically carries a much higher fee than linking your bank account directly.
- **Use each platform's built-in "recurring buy" / auto-invest feature** rather than manually buying each month — this is usually the cheapest way to execute and removes the temptation to time the market.
- **Avoid the "basic" trading view fees** where possible — on Coinbase, for example, the simple buy button costs more than using Advanced Trade for the same purchase.
- **Watch the spread, not just the stated fee** — some apps (like Robinhood) advertise "zero commission" but build their margin into the buy/sell spread, so compare the effective price you're paying against the market price.

## Bottom line
For someone new to crypto in NY who wants simplicity and low fees for small recurring BTC/ETH purchases, **Coinbase** or **Gemini** are the most well-rounded choices — both are fully NYDFS-licensed, beginner-friendly, and have solid recurring-buy tools. If you want the absolute simplest "set and forget" experience and don't mind giving up some control, **Robinhood** is also excellent. If Bitcoin is your main focus, **Strike** is worth a look for its low-cost recurring purchase model.

prompt: I'm 23 and rebuilding my credit after a few missed payments. I can only put down a small deposit and I want to move to a regular unsecured card within a year. Recommend secured credit cards.
text:
Given your situation — rebuilding after missed payments, a small deposit budget, and wanting to graduate to an unsecured card within a year — here are the secured cards that best fit:

## Top Picks for Low Deposit + Fast Graduation

**1. Capital One Platinum Secured Credit Card** — Best overall fit for you
A $49, $99 or $200 minimum refundable deposit opens your account, and you could earn back your deposit and upgrade to an unsecured card. Once approved, you'll have 35 days to make the minimum deposit of $49, $99 or $200, which is determined by your creditworthiness, but you will receive the minimum initial credit line of at least $200 regardless. The upgrade path is real: the Capital One Platinum Secured card can graduate to unsecured if you pay your monthly bill on time and otherwise manage your account responsibly. There's also an automatic credit limit review and upgrade check-in around the **6-month mark**, per NerdWallet's review.

**2. Discover it® Secured Cash Back**
This card recently cut its deposit requirement too: the Discover it Secured Cash Back credit card now features a security deposit requirement as low as $49 if you qualify, whereas previously, the minimum was $200. It also has a built-in review process: the issuer promises automatic monthly reviews for a potential transition to an unsecured account after seven months. That's well within your one-year window. One caveat worth noting: Discover it Secured Cash Back Credit Card accounts will be reviewed periodically for potential graduation, but Discover no longer promises automatic account reviews at the seven-month mark — so confirm current terms before applying. It also earns cash back while you rebuild, which the Capital One card doesn't.

**3. OpenSky® Secured Visa** — if you're worried about approval odds
Since you have missed payments on your record, this is a good backup: if you're looking for one of the easiest secured cards to qualify for, OpenSky stands out — it requires no credit check and has a minimum deposit of $200 with a maximum of $3,000. The tradeoff is a higher minimum deposit than the two cards above, and it carries an annual fee (around $35).

**4. Capital One Quicksilver Secured Cash Rewards** (if you want rewards + upgrade path)
With responsible card use, you may be upgraded to the unsecured Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards Credit Card and have your security deposit returned — plus it earns flat-rate cash back while secured.

## Quick Comparison

| Card | Min Deposit | Annual Fee | Graduation Timeline | Credit Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Capital One Platinum Secured | $49–$200 | $0 | ~6 months (automatic review) | Yes |
| Discover it Secured | $49–$200 | $0 | ~7 months (automatic review, verify current terms) | Yes |
| OpenSky Secured Visa | $200 | ~$35 | Case-by-case | **No** |
| Capital One Quicksilver Secured | $200 | $0 | Case-by-case, with rewards | Yes |

## My Recommendation for Your Situation

Given the small deposit and recent missed payments, I'd suggest **Capital One Platinum Secured** as your first application. It has the lowest possible deposit floor ($49), no annual fee, and Capital One is known for being relatively lenient with approvals even after credit dings. If you get declined due to the recent missed payments, **OpenSky** is your no-credit-check fallback.

## To Actually Hit Your 1-Year Unsecured Goal

Regardless of which card you pick, the issuer's graduation decision comes down to behavior, not just time. The general advice across issuers: a deposit-backed card is a powerful tool, but it's not the only step in rebuilding your credit — using your card responsibly, keeping your balance low, making on-time payments, and avoiding maxing out your limit demonstrates creditworthiness.

Practical checklist for your 12-month timeline:
- **Never miss a payment** — this is the single biggest factor given your history
- **Keep utilization under 30%** (ideally under 10%) of your limit each statement
- **Set up autopay** for at least the minimum so a slip-up never happens again
- **Avoid applying for multiple cards at once** — one hard inquiry is enough for now
- **Check at the 6-month mark** whether your issuer has reviewed you for graduation, and call to ask directly if they haven't

One nuance: whether you get automatically upgraded or not, your deposit is always refundable once you close or graduate the account, so there's no real downside to starting now other than tying up that initial $49–$200 for a few months.

**YouTube TV** (~$82.99/month) is widely considered the best all-around pick — it includes ESPN, unlimited cloud DVR, and an optional Sports Plus add-on (about $10.99/month) for NFL RedZone and extra sports networks. **Fubo** (~$80+/month) is the top pick if you follow multiple leagues seriously. Fubo started as a soccer-only streaming service and has evolved into the most aggressively sports-focused cable replacement on the market, going all-in on live games rather than balancing news and entertainment. It's especially strong for international soccer fans and viewers needing specific regional sports networks (beIN Sports, TUDN, RSNs).

## Best for Regional Sports Networks (RSNs)
**DIRECTV** stands out here. DIRECTV carries the most extensive RSN lineup of any live TV streaming service, with a MyHomeTeam add-on delivering in-market regional networks including Marquee Sports Network, Chicago Sports Network and Altitude Sports. Plans start around $64.99/month for the MySports package.

## Best Budget Option
**ESPN Select** (~$12.99-13/month) is a great value pick. It includes ESPN+ content and some live games, making it ideal for budget-conscious fans looking to supplement other services — offering a massive amount of live sports content for a low monthly price.

## ESPN Standalone (Full Access)
If you specifically want ESPN without a cable-style bundle, **ESPN Unlimited** (~$29.99-31.99/month) gives you everything: NFL, NBA, WNBA, NHL, MLB, college sports, soccer, tennis, golf, lacrosse and cricket. ## Budget Live TV Option
**Sling TV** is the cheapest entry point. Sling (Orange) starts around $45.99/month and is the cheapest way to get ESPN in a live bundle.

## Quick Recommendation Guide
- **Just want the easiest, most balanced option?** → YouTube TV
- **Follow multiple leagues/international soccer?** → Fubo
- **Care about local/regional teams?** → DIRECTV
- **On a tight budget but want live sports?** → ESPN Select or Sling TV

**Fubo** – The most sports-focused of the bundles. Fubo started as a soccer-only streaming service and has evolved into the most aggressively sports-focused cable replacement on the market, going all-in on live games while competitors try to balance news, entertainment, and sports. Outside of DirecTV Stream, Fubo is the only major streaming service committed to carrying Regional Sports Networks. A newer "Fubo Sports" tier launched too — a focused offering at a lower price that comes with 20-plus sports and broadcast networks featuring both national and local pro and college team coverage, including ESPN Unlimited.

**YouTube TV** – The most balanced all-around pick. For most sports fans, YouTube TV is the easiest all-around pick — ESPN included, unlimited cloud DVR, and an optional Sports Plus add-on (about $10.99/month, as of July 2026) for NFL RedZone and extra sports networks.

**DIRECTV** – Best for regional/local teams. DIRECTV carries the most extensive RSN lineup of any live TV streaming service, and the MyHomeTeam add-on for the DIRECTV MySports Genre Pack ($19.99/mo.) delivers in-market regional networks including Marquee Sports Network, Chicago Sports Network and Altitude Sports.

**Hulu + Live TV** – Good value if you also want Disney+/ESPN+ bundled in, pairing a solid live sports lineup with massive on-demand libraries and the Disney bundle for casual viewers.

**Sling TV** – Cheapest entry point. Sling is the cheapest door into live sports streaming, and it is the cheapest way to get full ESPN access if a live TV bundle's other channels would go unused.

## Standalone Sports Apps (Best for Budget/Specific Leagues)

**ESPN Unlimited** – Covers NFL, NBA, WNBA, NHL, MLB, college sports, soccer, tennis, golf, lacrosse and cricket, starting around $29.99–$31.99/month.

**Peacock** – One of the best streaming services for sports fans who want NBC's live sports coverage at a lower monthly price than a full live TV package. It won't give you every sports channel the way Fubo or DIRECTV can, but it offers a deep live sports lineup for a much lower monthly cost, covering NFL, NBA, Premier League, and more.

**Paramount+** – Has grown into a serious contender for live sports, headlined by its massive addition of UFC coverage, plus NFL on CBS and Champions League.

- **Want it all / die-hard fan:** Fubo or DIRECTV (best RSN coverage)
- **Most balanced/easiest overall:** YouTube TV
- **Tightest budget:** Sling TV or Peacock
- **Only care about ESPN content:** ESPN Unlimited standalone app
- **NFL on CBS/UFC/Champions League:** Paramount+

Note: no single service carries every league, so the right pick comes down to which sports you actually watch — if your team lives on one network, a standalone app is often cheaper than a full bundle. It's worth checking which networks carry your specific leagues before committing, since broadcasting rights shift year to year.

## 3. OpenSky® Secured Visa® — Best if you're worried about the credit check itself
If you're concerned the missed payments could trigger a denial even for a secured card, OpenSky removes that risk. OpenSky is unique because it doesn't require a credit check to apply. The minimum deposit is $200, and your credit limit equals your deposit (up to $3,000). It also reports to all three bureaus, which is essential for rebuilding. The trade-off: no rewards, and a $35 annual fee is typical, plus graduation tends to be slower/request-based rather than automatic.

## My suggestion given your specifics
- **If approvable:** Go with **Discover it Secured** — the ~7-month automatic review timeline directly matches your "within a year" goal, it's $0 annual fee, and you get cash back as a bonus while rebuilding.
- **If you want rock-bottom deposit cost:** **Capital One Platinum Secured** ($49 possible) with a clean graduation path.
- **If you're unsure you'll pass a credit check:** **OpenSky**, as a fallback that guarantees entry regardless of your recent missed payments — then plan to transition to a rewards unsecured card once your score recovers.

A few practical tips regardless of which you pick: keep utilization low (under 30%, ideally under 10%), set up autopay for at least the minimum to avoid another missed payment, and check your card issuer's app for built-in FICO tracking — several of these cards (Discover, Citi) include it for free, which will help you monitor your progress toward that one-year unsecured goal.

prompt: I just cut cable and live in Chicago. I mostly want NFL Sundays and local NBA games and would rather not pay more than $80 a month. Recommend streaming services for live sports.
text:
Here's the landscape for cord-cutters in Chicago who want NFL Sundays + Bulls games, based on current (Nov 2026) pricing:

## The challenge
Local Bulls broadcasts moved to **Chicago Sports Network (CHSN)**, and that's the tricky part — YouTube TV, Hulu + Live TV and Sling TV do not carry Chicago Sports Network. Only Fubo and DirecTV Stream carry it as a live-TV bundle, or you can get CHSN as a standalone app.

## Best fit for your budget: Fubo "Sports" + My Local Sports add-on
This is the sweet spot for exactly what you want:

Fubo Sports with My Local Sports is the cheapest live TV package that gets you CHSN alongside most of the channels Chicago sports fans need. For $74.98 per month after the first month, you get CHSN, Marquee Sports Network, ABC, CBS, FOX, NBC, ESPN, ESPN2, FS1, Big Ten Network and ESPN Unlimited.

That single package checks every box:
- **NFL Sundays**: local CBS and FOX (early/late afternoon games), NBC (Sunday Night Football), plus ESPN/ABC for Monday Night Football.
- **Bulls local games**: CHSN carries the vast majority of the schedule — CHSN (in-market only) access to Bulls games is available for $20/month as a standalone, but it's bundled into this Fubo tier.
- **Price**: $74.98/mo — under your $80 ceiling.

Note: Fubo's bigger "Pro" plan (which also includes CHSN) now runs $88.99/month plus a regional sports fee, so you'd want to stick with the Sports + Local Sports add-on tier specifically, not Pro.

## Even cheaper alternative: Antenna + CHSN app
If you want to shave costs further:
- A basic HD antenna pulls in local CBS, FOX, NBC, and ABC for free — in the Chicago area, an antenna picks up Chicago Sports Network on 62.2 and 62.3, which covers 75 of 80 games too.
- Add the **CHSN direct app** for the CHSN app for $19.99/month ($29.99 if also interested in Blackhawks games).
- Total: under $20/month, though you'd lose ESPN (Monday Night Football) unless you add something like ESPN+ separately, and antenna reception can vary by location in the city.

## What to skip
- **YouTube TV / Hulu + Live TV** ($82.99–$89.99/mo) — both already blow past your $80 budget on their own, and neither carries CHSN anyway, so you'd still need a separate Bulls workaround.
- **NFL Sunday Ticket** (for out-of-market games) isn't necessary here — you only need local CBS/FOX/NBC/ESPN coverage, which any of the above already includes. Sunday Ticket is a $300+/season add-on only needed if you want every out-of-market game.

**Bottom line:** Fubo's Sports plan + My Local Sports add-on (~$75/month) is the cleanest single-subscription solution that covers NFL Sundays and Bulls games locally while staying under $80. If you're willing to juggle two apps, an antenna + standalone CHSN app gets you there for a fraction of the price.

prompt: I'm 23 and rebuilding my credit after a few missed payments. I can only put down a small deposit and I want to move to a regular unsecured card within a year. Recommend secured credit cards.
text:
## Secured Credit Cards for Rebuilding Credit (Low Deposit + Fast Graduation Path)

Given your situation — small deposit, want to graduate to unsecured within a year — here are the top picks:

### 1. **Capital One Platinum Secured Credit Card** — *Best for lowest deposit*
- To open this card, you'll need to make a refundable minimum security deposit of $49, $99 or $200 online or by phone, and your initial credit limit starts at $200 regardless of deposit amount.
- You can pay your security deposit in a single payment or in installments (over a 35-day period), which is helpful if even $49 upfront is tight.
- It offers automatic credit line reviews, and you can prequalify with no hard credit check.
- Graduation path: You could be upgraded to the unsecured Capital One Platinum Credit Card after a period of responsible card use, with automatic consideration for a higher credit line in as little as 6 months with no additional deposit needed.
- No rewards — this card does not offer rewards — but it's purely a credit-building tool with minimal cost.

### 2. **Discover it® Secured Cash Back** — *Best if you want rewards while rebuilding*
- As of the September 2026 relaunch under Capital One ownership, the minimum security deposit is now as low as $49 instead of a flat $200... tiered by creditworthiness, down from a flat $200 before.
- It actually pays you back: Discover will automatically match all the cash back you've earned at the end of your first year! There's no minimum spending or maximum rewards.
- Important caveat: this card **paused new applications** earlier in 2026 during the Capital One integration, then relaunched in September. Discover paused new applications for this card on June 2, 2026 during its integration into Capital One (which acquired Discover in 2025). Capital One relaunched the card around September 10, 2026 with a new rewards structure and a lower minimum deposit. Double-check it's currently open for applications when you apply.
- Graduation: historically once you've been a cardholder for seven months, Discover will review your account and consider returning your security deposit — though note one source says Discover advertised automatic reviews starting at 7 months, and Capital One is retiring that promise. Upgrades are still possible, since Capital One says it reviews secured accounts periodically for graduation to an unsecured line.

### 3. **OpenSky® Secured Visa®** — *Best if your credit is too damaged for a credit check*
- It is the easiest secured credit card to qualify for because it requires no credit check and approves applicants with very poor or no credit history. You'll need a $200 minimum deposit and can expect approval within hours.
- Downside: you'll also need to pay a $35 annual fee on top of that deposit, and graduation isn't guaranteed the way it is with Capital One/Discover.

### Bottom Line for Your Goal (small deposit + unsecured in ~1 year)

**Best combo:** Start with the **Capital One Platinum Secured** — you can get in for as little as $49 (paid in installments if needed), and Capital One does **automatic reviews every 6 months** for a credit line increase/upgrade, giving you a real shot at graduating to unsecured well within a year if you keep utilization low and pay on time.

If you want cash back while you rebuild and can scrape together closer to $200, **Discover it Secured** is the stronger pick overall — just confirm it's accepting applications when you apply since it only recently reopened.

**Key habits to actually graduate within 12 months:** keep utilization under 30% (ideally under 10%), never miss a payment, and don't close the account even after approval for an unsecured product until the deposit is refunded.

prompt: We're a couple, one of us is vegetarian, we have about 30 minutes to cook on weeknights and want to stay around $12 a serving. Recommend meal kit delivery services.
text:
Here's a solid lineup of meal kit services that fit your criteria—especially the "one vegetarian, one not" dynamic, since the best fit for you is a service that lets each of you pick a different recipe per week (rather than forcing the same dish for both servings).

## Top Picks

**HelloFresh** — Best all-around fit for a budget-conscious couple
Price per serving runs $8.99-$12.49 after the initial promotion, with vegetarian, pescatarian and low-calorie options. It's also noted for having a large, rotating vegetarian menu each week, which matters since you'll want fresh veg options regularly rather than the same 2-3 recipes on repeat. Most recipes are designed around a 30-40 min window, and you can filter by "Easy/Quick" tags.

**Home Chef** — Best value + biggest vegetarian selection
Home Chef has more than 270 vegetarian options in the catalog, and it has the lowest starting price per serving for dinners, starting at $6.99 per serving. This is a strong pick for mixed-diet couples because you can select vegetarian and non-vegetarian meals in the same order, each sized for 2 servings.

**Green Chef** — Best if you want organic + couple-sized portions
Green Chef was specifically called out as Best Vegetarian Meal Delivery Service for Couples, and it offers three to eight recipes per week for two, four or six people with a vegetarian-friendly option. Organic ingredients push it toward the higher end of your budget, but it often runs in the $11-13/serving range after discounts.

**EveryPlate** — Best if you want to stretch the budget further
EveryPlate is more affordable than many meal services, with meals starting at $4.99 per serving because it uses less packaging and simple ingredients. It has a smaller menu than HelloFresh, so vegetarian variety is more limited, but it leaves lots of room in your $12/serving cap for add-ons or occasional splurges.

**Purple Carrot** — If you want a *fully* vegetarian/vegan-forward menu (not just add-on options)
Purple Carrot runs about $14.25 per serving, which is a bit over your target, but it's worth a mention since if you're vegan and looking for a meal kit service, Purple Carrot is not just your best bet, it's also one of your only options. Since only one of you is vegetarian, you may not need a fully plant-based service, but it's good to know it exists if you want more adventurous veg-forward cooking than the "one vegetarian option per week" you get from omnivore-focused services.

## How to Make the Numbers Work for a Couple

A few practical tips given your constraints:

- **Order 2 different recipes, 2 servings each, per delivery** on HelloFresh or Home Chef rather than ordering 1 recipe at 4 servings — this way one of you gets a vegetarian dish and the other doesn't have to eat vegetarian every night.
- **Filter by cook time.** HelloFresh, Home Chef, and Green Chef all let you filter recipes by prep time (often tagged "Quick," "15-minute," or "Easy Prep"), which should get you reliably under 30 minutes.
- **Watch for shipping fees**, which aren't always included in the advertised per-serving price — shipping can run $9.99 or $11.99 depending on location on some services, which can push a $10/serving box closer to $12-13 once split across just 4-6 servings a week.
- **Subscription discounts matter.** Most of these prices are promotional/first-box rates; ongoing weekly pricing is often a few dollars more per serving, so double check the "standard" (non-promo) price before committing if staying under $12 is a hard limit.

My overall recommendation: **start with HelloFresh or Home Chef** since both are well under your $12/serving target at baseline pricing, have deep vegetarian catalogs (so the vegetarian partner isn't stuck with the same 2 dishes), and are well-regarded for quick, approachable recipes that fit a 30-minute weeknight window.

2. **Set up autopay** for at least the minimum, given your history of missed payments — this is the single biggest lever for your score.
3. **Don't apply for multiple secured cards at once** — one hard inquiry is enough; stacking applications will ding you further.
4. **Ask about the graduation review proactively** around month 5–6 if the issuer hasn't flagged you automatically.
5. **Keep the account open** even after you get an unsecured card elsewhere, since account age matters for your score — unless the issuer refunds your deposit and closes it automatically upon graduation.

text:
Here's a rundown of meal kit services that fit well for a vegetarian/non-vegetarian couple cooking in ~30 minutes and staying near $12/serving:

## Top Picks

**HelloFresh — Best overall for a mixed-diet couple**
HelloFresh is rated as the best vegetarian meal kit delivery company, with more than a dozen weekly vegetarian dishes, while still offering plenty of meat-based options for your partner. Pricing is right in your target range — HelloFresh offers over 100 weekly recipes with a variety of dietary options, with pricing starting at $11.99 per serving. It's also well-suited to time-crunched weeknights, since it has a huge menu of rotating options with vegetarian, pescatarian and low-calorie options.

**Home Chef — Best for flexibility + speed**
Home Chef is a meal kit and prepared meal delivery service that ships food to most of the continental USA and is specifically noted as the best vegetarian meal delivery service for families because of the variety offered (works just as well for couples). It's also on the cheaper end — Home Chef's meal kits start at $8.99 per serving and include various options, such as meal kits, 15-minute meal kits, oven-ready meal kits — meaning it's easy to stay under $12/serving while also grabbing their quick-prep kits for busy weeknights.

**EveryPlate — Best if you want extra budget cushion**
If you want room to splurge on a nicer bottle of wine, EveryPlate is the cheapest mainstream option: EveryPlate costs $6.99 per serving, regardless of box size, and it does offer vegetarian recipes, though the menu variety is more limited than HelloFresh or Home Chef.

## Good, Slightly Pricier Options (still near your $12 ceiling)

**Green Chef — Best if you want organic + dedicated veg menus**
Green Chef is a USDA-certified organic meal kit delivery service that offers dedicated vegetarian and vegan menus, and it's noted for high quality ingredients, many of which are pre-chopped, making meal assembly a breeze — handy for a 30-minute cook time. The catch: pricing tends to sit right at or slightly above your budget, ranging from $11.99-$13.99 per serving.

**Purple Carrot — Best if the non-vegetarian partner is open to all-plant-based nights occasionally**
Purple Carrot takes the (vegan) cake as the best overall vegan meal delivery service, as it offers both meal kits and prepared meals for subscribers. Since vegan meals are automatically vegetarian-friendly, this is a clever way to simplify cooking for a mixed household on nights you want to eat the same thing. Pricing runs a bit above $12 typically, so watch your box selections.

## A Practical Note on Budgeting

Keep in mind that the per-serving price is only one of three line items — on top of it, expect shipping of typically $8–$11 per delivery unless the service waives it. So to truly stay at "$12/serving," factor shipping into your math: for a 2-person, 3-meal week (6 servings), a $10 shipping fee adds roughly $1.67/serving on top of the sticker price. HelloFresh and Home Chef are your safest bets to land all-in around $12–13/serving after shipping, especially if you choose their 3-meals-per-week plans rather than daily delivery.

## Recommended Starting Point
Given your constraints (couple, one vegetarian, 30 min, ~$12/serving), **I'd start with HelloFresh or Home Chef** — both let one of you pick vegetarian recipes and the other pick meat-based ones from the *same weekly box*, both advertise fast-prep options, and both land comfortably in your price range even after shipping.

**HelloFresh** – The most popular all-around choice for mixed-diet couples. HelloFresh is rated the best vegetarian meal kit delivery company, with more than a dozen weekly vegetarian dishes alongside plenty of meat options for your non-vegetarian partner. Pricing runs starting at $11.99 per serving, right at your target, and it offers 2-serving box sizes.

**Home Chef** – Great flexibility and value. Home Chef offers customizable meal kits and oven-ready options with clearly labeled vegetarian and calorie-conscious recipes. It's also one of the cheaper mid-tier options, with meal kits starting at $8.99 per serving and including 15-minute meal kits, oven-ready meal kits, and grill-ready meal kits — ideal if you want something even faster than 30 minutes on busy nights.

**Green Chef** – Best specifically for couples. Fortune names it the Best Vegetarian Meal Delivery Service for Couples, and it's the first meal kit service certified by the CCOF (California Certified Organic Farmers) if organic matters to you. It runs slightly above your budget at $11.99–$13.99 per serving, so watch portion/box size to stay near $12.

**EveryPlate** – If you want room under your $12 cap for occasional splurges elsewhere, this is the value pick. EveryPlate is the Best Budget Vegetarian Meal Delivery Service, with pricing as low as roughly $4.99–$6.99 per serving — significantly lower than HelloFresh or Home Chef. Recipes are simpler (less packaging, fewer specialty ingredients) but still deliver quick, straightforward dinners.

**Purple Carrot** – Worth considering if the vegetarian partner wants fully plant-based meals rather than just meatless ones. The service has 2- and 4-serving options and stands out among the leading vegan-friendly meal delivery services nationwide, though it runs a bit pricier at $9 to $15 per serving depending on the dish.

## A Few Practical Notes

- **Watch shipping fees**: Per-serving price isn't the whole story — a meal kit costs an average of $9.99 per serving in starting price, ranging from $5.99 to $13.99, with shipping typically $8–$11 per delivery unless the provider waives it. For a 2-person household, shipping adds meaningfully to your per-serving cost, so factor that into the $12 target.
- **Two-serving plans cost more per meal**: Most of these services charge the *same* per-serving price regardless of box size, but shipping gets split across fewer servings when you order for 2 instead of 4, so your real cost may run higher than the advertised rate.
- **Prep time**: For a guaranteed 30-minutes-or-under experience, specifically filter for "Quick & Easy" (HelloFresh), "15-Minute Meals" (Home Chef), or "Fast & Fresh" lines — not every recipe in a given service's rotation hits that mark.

**My recommendation**: Start with **HelloFresh or Home Chef** — both sit right around your $12/serving target, have robust vegetarian menus alongside meat options (so you're not ordering two separate kits), and offer fast-prep recipe tags for weeknights. If budget is the tighter constraint, **EveryPlate** gives you the most cushion.

Here's a breakdown based on what matters most to you—budget, specific leagues, or comprehensive coverage:

### 🏆 Best All-Around Pick: **YouTube TV**
YouTube TV is the best live TV streaming service for most people. It's particularly strong for sports because:
- YouTube TV (about $82.99/month, as of July 2026) is the most balanced pick: ESPN included, unlimited cloud DVR, and a $10.99/month Sports Plus add-on for NFL RedZone and extra sports networks.
- YouTube TV now also offers a **dedicated Sports plan**: The YouTube TV sports plan starts at $65/month (or $55/month for new users), including the major sports channels from the larger package: local stations, ESPN, the recently relaunched NBC Sports Network, etc.
- This sports-only tier includes roughly 30 channels, including the biggest local channels (ABC, CBS, Fox and NBC affiliates), ESPN Networks, sports-heavy cable channels TBS, TNT and USA, and league or sport-specific channels like Big Ten Network, Golf Channel, NBA TV and NFL Network.

### 🥅 Best for Die-Hard/Multi-League Fans: **Fubo**
If you follow several leagues or need regional sports networks:
- Fubo started as a soccer-only streaming service and has evolved into the most aggressively sports-focused cable replacement on the market, going all-in on live games rather than balancing news and entertainment.
- Fubo has the deepest sports channel lineup if you follow more than one league seriously.
- Its full sports lineup includes ABC, ACC Network, Big Ten Network, CBS, CBS Sports Network, ESPN, ESPN+, ESPN2, ESPNEWS, ESPNU, ESPN Unlimited, Fox, Fox News Channel, FS1, FS2, PGA Tour, SEC Network, Tennis Channel and the CW.

### 📺 Best for Regional Sports Networks: **DIRECTV**
If local teams (MLB, NBA, NHL) matter most:
- DIRECTV offers the most regional sports networks of any live TV streaming service, comparable to other major services on price, with Genre Packs covering just about every slice of streaming TV you could want.
- The MyHomeTeam add-on delivers in-market regional networks including Marquee Sports Network, Chicago Sports Network and Altitude Sports.

### 💰 Best Budget Options
- **Sling TV**: Sling is the cheapest door into live sports streaming, with Orange leaning into ESPN/Disney sports.
- **ESPN Unlimited (standalone app)**: Streams everything on ESPN's linear channels plus its exclusive content, without a cable login, for about $29.99/month (or a $35.99/month bundle with Disney+ and Hulu). Great as a supplement rather than a full replacement.
- **Peacock**: Starting around $12.99/month, good for Olympics, NFL, and NBA coverage plus Premier League soccer.

### ⚽ Best for Soccer/International Sports: **Fubo**
Fubo's channel lineup often includes a deep selection of regional sports networks, making it one of the few streaming options for watching certain local pro teams in baseball, basketball, and hockey, plus strong international soccer coverage via beIN Sports and TUDN.

### Other notable mentions
- **Hulu + Live TV** (~$90-99/mo): A strong all-in-one bundle that pairs live sports with Disney+/ESPN+ content and massive on-demand libraries.
- **Paramount+**: Has grown into a serious contender for live sports, headlined by its massive addition of UFC coverage, plus NFL on CBS, NWSL, and Champions League soccer.

---

**Bottom line:** For most people, **YouTube TV** offers the best balance of price, ESPN access, and DVR features. If you're a serious multi-sport fan or need regional networks, **Fubo** or **DIRECTV** are worth the extra cost. If you just want one specific league/network, a standalone app like **ESPN Unlimited** or **Paramount+** can save significant money.

Fubo's service focuses primarily on channels that distribute live sports. Fubo started as a soccer-only streaming service and has evolved into the most aggressively sports-focused cable replacement on the market, and outside of DirecTV Stream, it's the only major streaming service committed to carrying Regional Sports Networks.
- **Price:** around $88.99/month for the Pro plan
- **Best for:** Fans who follow multiple leagues and want the deepest channel lineup, including local teams

## 🥈 YouTube TV — Best All-Around Pick
For most sports fans, YouTube TV is the easiest all-around pick — ESPN included, unlimited cloud DVR, and an optional Sports Plus add-on (about $10.99/month) for NFL RedZone and extra sports networks.
- **Price:** starting around $82.99/month
- **Downside:** Limited Regional Sports Network (RSN) coverage

## 🥉 Hulu + Live TV — Best All-in-One Bundle
Hulu + Live TV pairs a solid live sports lineup with massive on-demand libraries and the Disney bundle for casual viewers. It bundles in Disney+ and ESPN+, making it a great value if you also want entertainment content alongside sports.

## 💰 Budget-Friendly Options

**Sling TV** — At about $45.99/month for the Orange plan, it's the cheapest way to get ESPN in a live bundle.

**ESPN Unlimited/Select** — For those on a budget, ESPN Select offers a massive amount of live sports content for a low monthly price and works well as a supplement to other services. Full ESPN Unlimited runs about $29.99-31.99/month and covers NFL, NBA, WNBA, NHL, MLB, college sports, soccer, tennis, golf, lacrosse and cricket.

**Peacock** — It won't give you every sports channel the way Fubo or DIRECTV can, but it does offer a deep live sports lineup for a much lower monthly cost, starting around $12.99/month and covering NFL, NBA, Premier League, and MLB.

## 📡 DIRECTV — Best for Regional Sports Networks
DIRECTV carries the most extensive RSN lineup of any live TV streaming service, with the MyHomeTeam add-on delivering in-market regional networks including Marquee Sports Network, Chicago Sports Network and Altitude Sports. Great if your priority is following local MLB/NBA/NHL teams.

---

Coinbase is an S&P 500 company holding a New York BitLicense, with free ACH funding, 300+ assets, and CFTC-regulated futures access. It has a simple recurring-buy feature that makes monthly DCA for BTC and ETH effortless, and transaction fees as low as 0.30% ($3.00 on a $1,000 purchase) via Coinbase's exchange/advanced interface. Using the simple "Buy" button costs more than the advanced trade tab, so set up recurring buys through Coinbase's advanced trading view to keep fees near that lower rate.

**2. Robinhood** — Best for low, flat fees
Robinhood offers commission-free mobile trading and is licensed in New York under a BitLicense. Robinhood brings a no-fee ethos to cryptocurrency trading, with fees between 0.03%-0.85% using smart exchange routing. It's a solid choice if you want crypto alongside other investments in one simple app.

**3. Gemini** — Best for security-first, New York-native feel
Gemini was founded in New York and is one of the only exchanges available in all 50 states. It runs as a New York-chartered trust company and hasn't reported a single major hack in eight years of operation, which gives extra peace of mind as a beginner. Fees are a bit higher if you use the simple "instant buy" feature — Gemini's instant buy fee, which most beginners would use, is about 1.47% — so look for Gemini's "ActiveTrader" mode for lower costs if you don't mind a slightly less simple interface.

**4. SoFi Crypto** — Simplest flat-fee option if you already bank with SoFi
SoFi members can buy, sell, and hold 27+ cryptocurrencies including Bitcoin and Ethereum, with a straightforward 1% fee on crypto trades and no monthly maintenance fees. It's a nationally chartered bank platform, so it's about as simple and low-stress as crypto buying gets.

You'll see Strike and River recommended a lot for cheap recurring buys — Strike and River charge no fee on recurring Bitcoin buys, though one-time purchases carry a fee plus a spread — but these are **Bitcoin-only**, so they won't work for your ETH purchases. For someone new to crypto who wants simplicity + low fees for both BTC and ETH:
- Start with **Coinbase** (easiest onboarding, trusted, works with bank ACH, and you can automate monthly recurring buys of both BTC and ETH in one place). Just be sure to use the "Advanced Trade" tab/fees rather than the basic "Buy" button to avoid the higher convenience fee.

Good news for your situation: since you're new to crypto and just want to **DCA (dollar-cost average) into BTC and ETH with low fees and minimal hassle**, New York actually narrows your choices in a helpful way — the state's strict BitLicense regime filters out a lot of the noise (no Binance.US, Kraken, Crypto.com, or KuCoin here). The New York State Department of Financial Services requires companies that conduct "virtual currency business activity" to obtain a BitLicense, and for this reason, many popular crypto exchanges — including Kraken, Crypto.com, and Binance.US — do not operate in New York State.

Here are the best fits for your specific needs:

## Top Recommendation: **Coinbase**
This is the easiest on-ramp for a beginner. It's the only major exchange available in all 50 states, including New York, thanks to its NYDFS BitLicense secured back in 2017. It has a clean recurring-buy feature for scheduling monthly BTC/ETH purchases, and if fees bother you, **Coinbase One** (a paid subscription) waives trading fees — worth it if you're buying every month, since otherwise standard fees run 0.84% trading fee plus 1% spread on basic buys.

## Strong Alternative: **Gemini**
Also New York-born and fully licensed. Gemini runs as a New York-chartered trust company and hasn't reported a single major hack in eight years of operation. It's a bit pricier for small/casual buys (0.0%–3.49% depending on payment method and platform), but its security reputation and simple interface make it a solid "set it and forget it" option.

## Best If You Want Rock-Bottom Fees on Just Bitcoin: **Strike or River**
If you decide you only want to DCA into Bitcoin (and handle ETH separately, or skip it), these Bitcoin-only apps are the cheapest around for recurring buys. Strike is an app designed specifically for buying and selling Bitcoin — one-time purchases carry a fee, but recurring purchases are free after the first week, making it a good fit for buying Bitcoin on a schedule. Similarly, River is a Bitcoin-only app where one-time orders carry a 1% fee, but recurring buys are free after the first week. The catch: since they're BTC-only, they won't work if you also want ETH in the same app.

## Other licensed options in NY (less ideal for your use case)
- **Robinhood**: offers some of the lowest fees for crypto buying, selling and trading at just 0.55%, and stands out by offering 0% fees on debit card deposits — a good low-fee alternative if you want a very simple app and don't mind it being a brokerage rather than a dedicated crypto platform.
- **Bitstamp**: one of the longest-running crypto exchanges, and it holds a New York BitLicense — reliable but less beginner-polished than Coinbase.
- **eToro**: switched on New York crypto trading in April 2026 — newer to the NY market, so less of a track record locally yet.

## Bottom line for your goals
For simplicity + both BTC and ETH + low ongoing hassle: **start with Coinbase** (pair it with Coinbase One if you're buying monthly to cut fees), and consider **Gemini** as a backup/comparison. If fees are your #1 priority and you're fine managing two apps, pair **Strike or River for BTC** with **Coinbase for ETH**.

One important warning: Binance.US explicitly lists New York under its unsupported states due to NYDFS regulations, and using a VPN to circumvent these restrictions may result in your account being suspended — so don't go that route even if you see it mentioned elsewhere online.

prompt: I'm 23 and rebuilding my credit after a few missed payments. I can only put down a small deposit and I want to move to a regular unsecured card within a year. Recommend secured credit cards.
text:
Given your situation—23, rebuilding after missed payments, small deposit, and wanting to graduate to unsecured within a year—here are the best-fit secured cards:

## Top Picks for Your Situation

**1. Capital One Platinum Secured Credit Card** — Best overall fit
This is the standout choice for a small deposit. A $49, $99 or $200 minimum refundable deposit opens your account, and you could earn back your deposit and upgrade to an unsecured card. Even better, you'll have 35 days to make the minimum deposit, which is determined by your creditworthiness, and you can submit more than the minimum to increase your credit line if you want to add cash later. It offers an automatic credit limit review after six months and a possible upgrade path to a traditional, unsecured card with Capital One. No annual fee, either.

**2. Discover it® Secured Cash Back**
Discover recently lowered its barrier to entry: the Discover it Secured Cash Back credit card now features a security deposit requirement as low as $49 if you qualify, whereas previously the minimum was $200. It also has a faster review cycle — automatic reviews starting at 7 months to see if you can transition to an unsecured line of credit with your deposit returned. Bonus: it actually pays cash back while you rebuild (rare for secured cards), and matches your first year of cash back earned.

**3. Secured Chime Credit Builder Visa® — if you want zero deposit at all**
If even $49 is tight right now, Chime's card is worth a look: there's no credit check to apply, no annual fees or interest, and no minimum security deposit required — the money you move into the secured account is the amount you can spend on your card. It won't build credit identically to a bank-reported secured card with a hard credit pull, but it's a solid zero-barrier option if cash is extremely limited.

**4. OpenSky® Secured Visa® — backup if you're worried about approval**
Since you mentioned missed payments, approval odds matter. OpenSky is useful because it doesn't require a credit check to apply, with a minimum deposit of $200, and your credit limit equals your deposit (up to $3,000). It does carry a $35 annual fee, and it doesn't have a built-in graduation path, so you'd eventually need to apply for a new unsecured card elsewhere rather than auto-upgrade.

## How to Actually Graduate Within a Year

Given your 12-month goal, I'd prioritize **Capital One Platinum Secured** or **Discover it Secured** specifically because of their graduation mechanics:

- Capital One reviews accounts as early as **6 months** for an automatic upgrade to unsecured credit, with your deposit refunded.
- Discover does **automatic reviews starting at 7 months**.

To make that upgrade happen on schedule:
1. **Keep utilization low** — ideally under 10-30% of your $200 limit, so spend roughly $20–$60/month max.
2. **Never miss a payment** — set up autopay for at least the minimum, ideally pay in full each cycle.
3. **Don't apply for other new credit** in the meantime — extra inquiries can work against you during the rebuilding phase.
4. **Check your free credit reports periodically** (via AnnualCreditReport.com) to confirm the card is reporting correctly and no old missed-payment marks are lingering inaccurately.

One practical note: since you had missed payments previously, a card with **no hard credit check** (OpenSky) could serve as a safety-net backup if you're denied by Capital One or Discover, but try the graduation-friendly options first since that's your primary goal.

Based on current market data (November 2026), here are the best secured card options for your situation — low deposit, no annual fee, and a real path to graduate to an unsecured card within about a year:

## Top picks

**1. Capital One Platinum Secured Credit Card — Best for your low-deposit need**
A $49, $99 or $200 minimum refundable deposit opens your account, and you could earn back your deposit and upgrade to an unsecured card. You'll have 35 days to make the minimum deposit, which is determined by your creditworthiness. Even if you qualify for the lowest $49 deposit, you will receive the minimum initial credit line of at least $200. It offers an automatic credit limit review after six months and a possible upgrade path to a traditional, unsecured card with Capital One. No annual fee.

**2. Discover it® Secured Cash Back — Best for building credit + earning rewards**
The card now has a minimum refundable deposit of $49 with a credit limit starting at $200. It also offers cash back rewards with a first-year match. For graduation, Discover promises automatic monthly reviews for a potential transition to an unsecured account after seven months. Note: accounts will be reviewed periodically for potential graduation to a regular card, but Discover no longer promises automatic account reviews at the seven-month mark — so verify current terms when you apply. No annual fee.

**3. OpenSky® Secured Visa® — Best if you're worried about a hard credit check**
OpenSky is one of the few secured cards that pays interest on your deposit, and can graduate to an unsecured product. OpenSky is unique because it doesn't require a credit check to apply. Deposit minimum is $200, but it does carry a $35 annual fee — something to weigh against the no-credit-check convenience.

**4. Citi® Secured Mastercard® — Good for tracking progress**
After 18+ months of on-time payments, you may be eligible to upgrade to an unsecured Citi card with a higher limit. This timeline is longer than the others, so it's a backup rather than a first choice if your goal is within a year.

## Why these fit your situation

- **Small deposit:** Capital One and Discover both let you start with as little as $49 and still get a $200 credit line, since refundable deposits as low as $49 unlock credit lines starting at $200, while a card's credit limit often doubles as the security deposit, though some issuers approve a $200 limit with a smaller deposit.
- **Rebuilding after missed payments:** Both are widely used specifically for this — a secured card is designed to offer you an opportunity to build or rebuild your credit with responsible use.
- **Graduating within a year:** Both Capital One (6 months) and Discover (7 months, pending current terms) have automatic review points well inside your one-year window, rather than cards like Citi that require 18+ months.

## Practical tips to actually graduate within a year

1. **Pay on time, every time** — this is the single biggest factor issuers look at before upgrading you.
2. **Keep utilization low** (ideally under 30%, better under 10%) even on a $200 limit — this disproportionately matters on small credit lines.
3. **Don't apply for multiple cards at once** — one secured card with consistent on-time payments does more for your score than several new accounts.
4. **Call and ask** — Capital One and Discover both do periodic automatic reviews, but you can often request a manual review once you hit the 6-7 month mark if your usage has been clean.
5. **Deposit more than the minimum if you can** — a $200 limit at $49 deposit is fine, but a slightly higher limit keeps your utilization ratio lower if your spending creeps up.

Given your specific situation — small deposit, rebuilding after missed payments, wanting to graduate within a year — I'd start with the **Capital One Platinum Secured** as your primary application, since it has the clearest low-deposit entry point and a documented sub-12-month upgrade path within the same card family.

Here's a rundown of the top streaming options for live sports in 2026, depending on what you're looking for:

## Full live TV bundles (best for most sports fans)

**YouTube TV** – YouTube TV is the best live TV streaming service for most people, and it offers a massive 100+ channel lineup and a multiview mode that makes it the undisputed king for households that watch a lot of live sports. It runs $82.99/month, and you can add a Sports Plus package for about $10.99/month for NFL RedZone and extra sports networks.

**Fubo** – Fubo started as a soccer-only streaming service and has evolved into the most aggressively sports-focused cable replacement on the market, going all-in on live games rather than balancing news and entertainment. It has the deepest live sports channel lineup of any bundle, which matters more if you follow several leagues rather than one. Plans range widely — from $19.99–$108.99/month with 59–303+ channels. One caveat: Fubo recently lost rights to NBC channels, a drawback since NBC carries Sunday Night Football and Premier League soccer.

**Hulu + Live TV** – Pairs a solid live sports lineup with massive on-demand libraries and the Disney bundle, good for casual viewers, running around $98.99/month.

**DIRECTV** – It offers the most regional sports networks and its Genre Packs cover just about every slice of streaming TV, carrying the most extensive RSN lineup of any live TV streaming service. A sports-focused option is DIRECTV MySports at $64.99/mo.

**Sling TV** – Sling is the cheapest door into live sports streaming, with Orange starting around $45.99 and offering about 30+ channels leaning into sports, ESPN and Disney with a single stream.

## Standalone/budget options

**ESPN (app)** – Now split into tiers: ESPN Select and ESPN Unlimited — Select costs $119.99/year, while Unlimited is $299.99/year for full streaming of every ESPN network and thousands of annual sporting events. ESPN Select offers a massive amount of live sports content for a low monthly price and works well as a supplement to other services.

**Paramount+** – It now includes access to every UFC fight, plus NFL games on CBS, Champions League soccer, NCAA basketball, and starts at $8.99/month for the ad-supported plan and $13.99/month for ad-free with SHOWTIME and access to live CBS 24/7.

**Peacock** – Combines exclusive theatrical releases with a massive sports hub essential for Olympics, NFL, and NBA coverage, starting around $12.99/month. It also holds Premier League rights.

## How to choose
- **Want everything in one place?** Go with YouTube TV or Fubo.
- **Specific league/niche?** ESPN Unlimited for college sports/UFC/NHL, Paramount+ for NFL-on-CBS/Champions League/UFC, Peacock for Premier League/Olympics/NBA.
- **On a budget?** Sling TV or ESPN Select as a supplement.
- **Regional sports networks (watching local MLB/NBA/NHL teams)?** Outside of DirecTV Stream, Fubo is the only major streaming service committed to carrying Regional Sports Networks.

A smart strategy many fans use: keep a service like Paramount+ active only during its season (e.g., August to February for NFL), then cancel until the next season starts — stacking cheaper standalone apps seasonally can beat paying for one expensive bundle year-round.

# Crypto Exchanges for Beginners in New York

New York has stricter regulations than other states (the "BitLicense"), which limits your options somewhat, but there are still solid platforms available to you.

## Top Recommendations

**Coinbase**
- Fully licensed in NY, very beginner-friendly interface
- Has a built-in recurring buy feature for DCA (dollar-cost averaging)
- Downside: Standard trading fees can be higher (~1.5-4% depending on payment method)
- Tip: Use **Coinbase Advanced Trade** (or the basic app's instant buy) — fees are much lower if you avoid the simple "Buy" button and use the advanced interface instead

**Kraken**
- Available in NY, respected for security track record
- Lower fees than basic Coinbase (~0.25-0.40% on regular trades)
- Supports recurring buys
- Interface is slightly less polished but still manageable

**Gemini**
- Founded by the Winklevoss twins, NY-based company, very compliance-focused
- Clean interface, has recurring purchase ("Gemini Dollar Cost Average") options
- Fees similar to Coinbase on the basic app; use **ActiveTrader** for lower fees

## Practical Tips to Keep Fees Low

1. **Avoid the "simple/instant buy" button** on any app — it often has the worst pricing. Look for "Pro," "Advanced," or "ActiveTrader" modes.
2. **Use limit orders** when possible instead of market orders (even a few cents savings adds up over time).
3. **Bank transfer (ACH)** instead of debit card/credit card — card payments often carry 3-4% fees vs ACH which can be free or near-free.
4. **Set up recurring buys** on whichever platform you choose — this automates your monthly purchases and removes emotion/timing decisions.

## My Suggestion for Simplicity

If you want the *easiest* overall experience: **Coinbase**, using their recurring buy feature with ACH bank transfer, accepting slightly higher fees for convenience.

If you want **lower fees** and don't mind a tiny bit more complexity: **Kraken**, setting up their recurring buy feature.

## One More Consideration

Once you're buying regularly, consider moving your crypto to a personal wallet (like a hardware wallet) rather than leaving it on the exchange — "not your keys, not your coins" is a common crypto principle for security. This isn't urgent for small amounts, but worth learning about as you get comfortable.

prompt: Recommend streaming services for live sports.
text:
Here's a current breakdown of the best streaming services for live sports, depending on your needs:

## Top Overall Picks

**YouTube TV** – YouTube TV is the best live TV streaming service for most people. It's the easiest all-around pick for sports fans — ESPN included, unlimited cloud DVR, and an optional Sports Plus add-on (about $10.99/month) for NFL RedZone and extra sports networks. It's also home to **NFL Sunday Ticket**, and the base plan includes NFL Network, with the optional "Sports Plus" add-on giving you NFL RedZone for commercial-free coverage.

**Fubo** – Fubo started as a soccer-only streaming service and has evolved into the most aggressively sports-focused cable replacement on the market, going all-in on live games rather than balancing news and entertainment. It carries the deepest live sports channel lineup of any bundle, which matters more if you follow several leagues rather than one. One caveat: TNT carries NBA playoff games that ESPN does not — which is why Fubo subscribers face a gap in postseason coverage.

**DIRECTV** – DIRECTV carries the most extensive RSN (regional sports network) lineup of any live TV streaming service, making it the top choice if you follow local teams closely.

## Budget/Standalone Options

**ESPN Unlimited** (the standalone ESPN app) – Access the full suite of ESPN linear networks and the entire ESPN+ library via ESPN Unlimited ($29.99/mo). Great if ESPN covers most of what you watch (NFL, NBA, college sports, UFC, etc.).

**Peacock** – Peacock Premium and Premium Plus caters to sports lovers and is a must-have for English Premier League fans and those who follow NBA. Starting around $12.99/month, it's a cheap add-on for select NFL, MLB, and NBA games plus the Olympics.

**Sling TV** – Sling is the cheapest door into live sports streaming, with Orange and Blue plans giving access to ESPN or FS1/NFL Network respectively at a lower price than full bundles.

**Paramount+** – Good if you want NHL, Bundesliga, La Liga, PGA Tour, UFL, and more — it's grown into a serious contender for live sports, headlined by its massive addition of UFC coverage.

## Bottom Line Recommendation

- **Want one all-around service?** → **YouTube TV** (best balance of price, DVR, and ESPN access)
- **Die-hard, multi-league fan who wants everything?** → **Fubo** (deepest channel lineup, strong RSN coverage)
- **Care most about local teams?** → **DIRECTV** (best RSN coverage)
- **Just want ESPN content without a big bundle?** → **ESPN Unlimited** ($29.99/mo standalone)
- **On a tight budget, want a supplement?** → **Peacock** or **Sling Orange**

Keep in mind that no single service carries all NFL games — you need multiple sources, and the same is largely true for other leagues like the NBA, since rights are split across networks (ESPN, NBC/Peacock, TNT/Max, Amazon Prime). Your best bet is identifying which specific teams/leagues matter most to you, then picking the service (or combo) that covers those.

prompt: I live in New York and I'm new to crypto. I want to buy small amounts of bitcoin and ether every month, keep fees low and keep things simple. Recommend cryptocurrency exchange platforms.
text:
Since you're in New York, your options are narrower than the rest of the US — state law (the **BitLicense**/NYDFS trust charter requirement) excludes several popular platforms like Kraken and Binance.US. Kraken skips New York and Maine, Crypto.com and Uphold skip New York, and staking availability varies by state everywhere. Binance does not possess a BitLicense, which is mandatory for cryptocurrency exchanges to operate in New York State, so it cannot legally serve New York residents.

Here are the platforms that are actually licensed for NY residents and work well for a simple "buy a little BTC and ETH every month" strategy:

## Top picks for you

**1. Coinbase — best overall for simplicity**
Coinbase has been fully licensed to operate in New York for years and is one of the most accessible and beginner-friendly crypto exchanges in the state. It has an easy recurring-buy feature. The catch: its simple buy/sell screen bundles a spread (around 1%) with a transaction fee that varies by payment method and can reach roughly 3.99% on card purchases. To keep fees low, fund via **ACH bank transfer** (free) rather than a debit/credit card, and if you're comfortable with a slightly less "simple" interface, use **Coinbase Advanced** instead of the basic app — its entry-tier fees are 0.50% maker / 0.90% taker, far cheaper than the simple-buy spread.

**2. Gemini — NY-born, strong compliance, good low-fee tier for small traders**
Gemini is one of the few crypto exchanges licensed to operate in New York, holding both a BitLicense and a New York trust charter. Its basic buy/sell interface isn't the cheapest (a 1.49% transaction fee for basic buy/sell orders, with an additional convenience fee of up to 1% depending on payment method), but if you use **Gemini ActiveTrader**, fees run roughly 0.00% maker and 0.20% taker at the entry tier — very cheap for small recurring buys once you learn the slightly more advanced interface.

**3. Robinhood Crypto — easiest/cheapest for pure simplicity**
Robinhood is a BitLicense-registered crypto exchange legally operating in New York and allows you to buy and sell cryptocurrencies commission-free, which is great if you're just getting started or want simple exposure to crypto prices. If your top priority is "simple and cheap" over having lots of advanced tools, this is hard to beat — no commissions, though there's a built-in spread on each trade.

## Honorable mentions
- **Bitstamp**: one of the longest-running crypto exchanges, holding a New York BitLicense, with maker/taker fees ranging from 0.40% down to 0.00% based on 30-day trading volume.
- **eToro**: switched on cryptoasset trading for New York residents on April 1, 2026, after becoming the first firm to receive a BitLicense from NYDFS following the FTX collapse — simple, social-trading focused, but fees are higher (around 1% buy/sell).

## My recommendation for your specific goal

Since you want **small monthly buys, low fees, and simplicity**:

1. **Start with Robinhood** if you want the absolute simplest "set it and forget it" experience with no commissions and a clean app.
