prompt: I live in New York and I'm new to crypto. I want to buy small amounts of bitcoin and ether every month, keep fees low and keep things simple. Recommend cryptocurrency exchange platforms.
text:
Great news — even though New York has some of the strictest crypto rules in the country (everything must be BitLicensed or hold a NY trust charter), there are still several solid, low-fee, beginner-friendly options that support recurring buys of both Bitcoin and Ether. Here's what I'd recommend:

## Best overall picks for you (BTC + ETH, low fees, simple recurring buys)

**1. Coinbase — Best all-around starting point**
If you're new to crypto and live in New York, Coinbase is a straightforward choice. The platform allows you to buy, sell, and store a wide range of cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, and a large selection of altcoins. Coinbase offers its full suite of trading features, including wallet transfers, recurring buys, and tax documentation. It's a long-standing, fully compliant platform — a long-time holder of a BitLicense, Coinbase has been fully licensed to operate in New York for years. Tip: use "Coinbase Advanced" (formerly Coinbase Pro) rather than the basic app — it has free ACH deposits tradable in minutes and much lower trading fees than the simple buy/sell interface.

**2. Gemini — New York–founded, strong compliance & security**
Gemini was founded in New York and is one of the only exchanges available in all 50 states. It holds the strongest regulatory status possible: Gemini is one of the few crypto exchanges licensed to operate in New York, holding both a BitLicense and a New York trust charter. It also has a low-fee mode for cost-conscious buyers — Gemini ActiveTrader is a strong low-fee choice for New Yorkers who trade often, available in New York as a Limited Liability Trust Company under New York Banking Law.

**3. Robinhood — Simplest, commission-free option**
Robinhood Crypto is licensed in New York under a BitLicense and lets New Yorkers buy and sell crypto with no commission. It's extremely easy to use and good for beginners, though Robinhood operates under a BitLicense, providing commission-free crypto trading but with significant limitations on wallet functionality — meaning it can be harder to withdraw crypto to your own wallet later if you want full self-custody.

## If you want the cheapest possible recurring buys (Bitcoin-focused)

If down the line you want to dollar-cost-average into Bitcoin specifically at near-zero fees, **Strike** is worth knowing about: one-time purchases carry a fee, but recurring purchases are free after the first week, which makes Strike a good fit for buying Bitcoin on a schedule. It recently became available in NY — NYDFS granted its operator, Zap Solutions, Inc., a BitLicense and money transmitter license in February 2026. The catch is it's Bitcoin-only, so you'd still need a second app (like Coinbase or Gemini) for Ether.

## What to avoid in New York

Several popular exchanges simply don't operate there, so don't waste time signing up: Kraken, Crypto.com, Binance.US, and KuCoin are not available in New York. Kraken skips New York and Maine, Crypto.com and Uphold skip New York.

## My practical recommendation for you

Given you want **simplicity + both BTC and ETH + low fees + monthly recurring buys**, I'd start with **Coinbase** or **Gemini**:
- Both are fully licensed, beginner-friendly, and support automatic recurring purchases of Bitcoin and Ethereum.
- Set up a small monthly recurring buy (e.g., $25–$100) via free ACH bank transfer — avoid debit card funding, which typically carries higher fees.
- Use the "advanced trade" mode on either platform (Coinbase Advanced / Gemini ActiveTrader) if you want to shave fees down further once you're comfortable, since the basic/simple buy interfaces usually have a built-in spread markup on top of the trading fee.

A reasonable approach: open an account on **Gemini or Coinbase**, link your bank account, and set a recurring buy split between BTC and ETH on whatever schedule fits your budget (weekly or monthly). That keeps things simple, keeps you fully compliant as a NY resident, and keeps fees reasonably low without needing multiple apps.

YouTube TV is the closest thing to a complete cable replacement, offering 100+ channels including ESPN, ESPN2, FS1, FS2, NBC Sports, CBS, ABC, and every local network. If you want a cheaper sports-focused option, YouTube TV also has a Sports Plan for $64.99/month with 30+ channels including ESPN, ESPN2, FS1, FS2, NBA TV, CBS Sports Network, TNT, TBS and NFL Network.

## 🔥 Fubo — Best for Die-Hard Sports Fans
Fubo started as a soccer-only streaming service and has evolved into the most aggressively sports-focused cable replacement on the market, going all-in on live games while competitors balance news, entertainment, and sports. It's especially strong for **Regional Sports Networks (RSNs)**: outside of DirecTV Stream, Fubo is the only major streaming service committed to carrying Regional Sports Networks.

## 📺 DIRECTV — Best for Local/Regional Teams
DIRECTV carries the most extensive RSN lineup of any live TV streaming service, with the MyHomeTeam add-on ($19.99/mo) delivering in-market regional networks including Marquee Sports Network, Chicago Sports Network and Altitude Sports.

## 💰 Budget Options
- **ESPN Unlimited** — starting at $29.99/month, covers NFL, NBA, WNBA, NHL, MLB, college sports, soccer, tennis, golf, lacrosse and cricket, and is the cheapest way to get ESPN content legally without a TV provider.

- **Paramount+** — starting at $8.99/month, covers NFL, NWSL, WNBA, UFC, college sports and select PGA Tour events, and has grown into a serious contender for live sports, headlined by its massive addition of UFC coverage.

## 🎬 Hulu + Live TV — Best for Bundled Entertainment
Hulu + Live TV costs around $89.99/month (with ads) and bundles Disney+ and ESPN Select into one price — great if you want sports plus a big on-demand library.

## My Recommendation
- **Most people:** YouTube TV — best all-around balance of price, sports coverage, and DVR features.
- **Serious multi-league fans / need RSNs:** Fubo or DIRECTV.
- **Just want ESPN cheaply:** ESPN Unlimited ($29.99/mo) as a standalone or supplement.
- **Budget-conscious with light sports needs:** Peacock or Paramount+.

Since pricing and lineups shift throughout the year, it's worth checking current promos before committing — and remember, no single service carries every league, so the right pick comes down to which sports you actually watch.

**Discover it® Secured Credit Card** — Known for rewards. A strong combination of features earned the Discover it® Secured Credit Card the title of "best card for building credit" in the NerdWallet Best-Of Awards every year from 2018 to 2026, and it was one of the first secured cards with rewards and a bonus offer.

## By Specific Need

**For a high credit limit:** The Platinum Secured Mastercard® from First Tech Federal Credit Union has a maximum credit limit of $25,000, and it also features a fairly low variable APR range. Alternatively, the BankAmericard® Secured credit card offers the potential for an exceptionally high credit limit for a secured card — up to $5,000.

**For no credit check:** If your current credit score is making it difficult to get a credit card, the Opensky® Plus Secured Visa® Credit Card doesn't require a credit check to apply.

**For no fees overall:** The DCU Visa® Platinum Secured Credit Card is frequently recommended for having no annual fee or extra charges.

## How Secured Cards Work
Whether you're building credit from scratch or rebuilding after a setback, a secured credit card can help. Secured cards require a cash security deposit, usually equal to your credit line, which makes them easier to qualify for. Additionally, because they don't rely on your creditworthiness and don't have a minimum credit score requirement, secured cards are easier to get approved for than traditional unsecured cards.

## Quick Recommendation Guide
- **New to credit / want low deposit:** Capital One Platinum Secured
- **Want rewards:** Discover it® Secured or Capital One Quicksilver Secured
- **Bad credit / need guaranteed approval:** Opensky® Secured Visa
- **Need a high limit:** First Tech FCU Platinum Secured or BankAmericard® Secured
- **Rebuilding after bankruptcy:** OpenSky® Secured Visa

A good rule of thumb: prioritize cards with **no annual fee**, that **report to all three credit bureaus**, and that offer a **path to upgrade** to an unsecured card after responsible use. Since offers and terms (APRs, deposit minimums, rewards) change frequently, it's worth checking issuer websites directly before applying for current rates and fees.

Based on current reviews and pricing, here are solid picks for a couple with one vegetarian, a ~30-minute weeknight window, and a target around $12/serving:

**HelloFresh** – Great fit for your budget and vegetarian needs. It offers around 10 weekly vegetarian menu options at $11.99 per serving, and it scales cleanly to 2-person servings. It's a mainstream kit known for straightforward, quick weeknight recipes.

**Home Chef** – Likely your best overall value. It stood out in testing for its extensive menu of vegetarian meals, with more than 270 vegetarian options in the catalog, and has the lowest starting price per serving on the list for dinners, starting at $6.99 per serving. prompt: I live in New York and I'm new to crypto. I want to buy small amounts of bitcoin and ether every month, keep fees low and keep things simple. Recommend cryptocurrency exchange platforms.
text:
Since you're in New York, your options are more limited than the rest of the country — New York requires exchanges to hold a **BitLicense** (or a trust charter) from the NYDFS, and popular platforms like Kraken, Crypto.com, Binance.US, and KuCoin are all unavailable to New York residents. Here are the best fits for your goal of simple, low-fee, recurring small purchases of BTC and ETH:

## Top picks for your use case

**1. Coinbase — best overall for beginners**
A long-time holder of a BitLicense, Coinbase has been fully licensed to operate in New York for years, and unlike some platforms that offer a limited version of their services in New York, Coinbase offers its full suite of trading features, including wallet transfers, recurring buys, and tax documentation. It's widely considered the easiest on-ramp for someone new to crypto, with a simple interface for setting up automatic weekly/monthly buys of BTC and ETH.

**2. Gemini — best for security-conscious, "set it and forget it" users**
Gemini is one of the few crypto exchanges licensed to operate in New York, holding both a BitLicense and a New York trust charter. It was actually the very first licensed Ethereum exchange based in the USA when it was approved in 2016, so ETH support is solid. On fees, Gemini ActiveTrader charges roughly 0.00% maker and 0.20% taker fees at the entry tier if you use the "ActiveTrader" order-book interface rather than the simple instant-buy screen (the instant-buy screen has a convenience fee built in, so it's worth learning the basic order-book flow once you're comfortable).

**3. Robinhood — simplest app experience, commission-free**
Robinhood is a BitLicense-registered crypto exchange legally operating in New York, meaning it meets all NYDFS regulatory requirements, and allows you to buy and sell cryptocurrencies commission-free, which is great if you're just getting started or want simple exposure to crypto prices. Forbes' 2026 testing rated it highly specifically for this exact use case: Robinhood is the best crypto exchange for recurring investments, with its recurring investment feature allowing dollar-cost averaging at a fractional level. Note that Robinhood's quoted price includes a spread rather than a visible commission, so the "0% fee" isn't quite fee-free in practice.

**4. Strike — if you mainly want low-cost recurring Bitcoin buys**
Strike is newer to New York but is built around automated recurring purchases. Recurring purchases lose the trading fee after their first week, leaving only the spread, and Strike received its BitLicense in 2026, with bill pay and loans also cleared for New York. It's more bitcoin-centric, but it does support ETH as well.

## Platforms to avoid in NY
Don't waste time signing up for the "big name" exchanges you may have heard of elsewhere — Kraken excludes New York and Maine, while Crypto.com excludes New York alone, and Binance and KuCoin don't serve NY residents either.

## My recommendation for you specifically
Given you want **simplicity + low fees + small recurring BTC/ETH buys**, I'd suggest starting with **Coinbase** (easiest UI, full recurring-buy support, very beginner-friendly) and keeping **Gemini** in mind as a backup or second account if you want slightly lower fees once you're comfortable using its order book instead of the "buy now" button. Robinhood is a great alternative if you already use it for stocks and want everything in one app.

A couple of practical tips regardless of platform:
- Fund purchases via **bank transfer/ACH** rather than debit/credit card — card funding usually carries a much higher fee.
- Set up the **recurring buy** feature (all of the above support it) rather than manually buying each month — it enforces discipline and often avoids extra "instant buy" fees.
- Since you're buying small amounts, watch out for flat minimum fees that can eat into tiny purchases — Gemini's ActiveTrader tier and Strike's no-fee-after-first-week recurring buys are specifically designed to minimize this.

Here's a breakdown of the best streaming services for live sports in 2026, based on current coverage, price, and the leagues they support.

## Best Overall / Most Popular
**YouTube TV** is widely considered the top all-around pick for cord-cutters. For most sports fans, YouTube TV is the easiest all-around pick — ESPN included, unlimited cloud DVR, and an optional Sports Plus add-on (about $10.99/month) for NFL RedZone and extra sports networks. It also stands out for NFL coverage, as YouTube TV is the best streaming service for NFL fans.

## Best for Die-Hard Sports Fans / Deepest Channel Lineup
**Fubo** is built specifically for sports fans. Fubo started as a soccer-only streaming service and has evolved into the most aggressively sports-focused cable replacement on the market, going all-in on live games while competitors balance news and entertainment. Fubo ($88.99) is the only service that offers local channels, RSNs, NFL Network, NBA TV, NHL Network, MLB Network, and NFL RedZone.

## Best for Regional Sports Networks (RSNs)
If you want to watch your local MLB, NBA, or NHL team, RSN access matters most. Outside of DirecTV Stream, Fubo is the only major streaming service committed to carrying Regional Sports Networks. **DIRECTV** leads here: DIRECTV carries the most extensive RSN lineup of any live TV streaming service, and the MyHomeTeam add-on for the DIRECTV MySports Genre Pack ($19.99/mo.) delivers in-market regional networks including Marquee Sports Network, Chicago Sports Network and Altitude Sports.

## Best Value / Budget Option
**Sling TV** is the cheapest entry point into live sports streaming. Sling (Orange) starts around $45.99 and is the cheapest way to get ESPN in a live bundle. For an even leaner option, ESPN Select was designated Best Bang for Your Buck for 2026, priced around $13/month with ESPN+ content and some live games — a massive amount of live sports content for a low monthly price that works well as a supplement to other services.

## Best All-in-One Value Bundle
**Hulu + Live TV** combines sports with a huge on-demand library. It pairs a solid live sports lineup with massive on-demand libraries and the Disney bundle for casual viewers. It's also strong for college sports: Hulu + Live TV is rated Best of the Best for College Sports.

## Best for Specific Leagues/Sports
- **Paramount+**: has grown into more than just a hub for streaming CBS hits — it's now a serious contender for live sports, headlined by its massive addition of UFC coverage, plus NFL, Champions League, and NWSL.
- **Peacock**: Good for exclusive theatrical releases from Universal Pictures and Focus Features combined with a massive sports hub essential for Olympics, NFL, and NBA coverage.
- **Apple TV**: isn't the best for general live sports coverage, but it's a worthy investment for fans of Major League Soccer, plus Formula 1 and MLB Friday Night Baseball.

## Quick Decision Guide
- **Want it all / follow multiple leagues:** Fubo or DIRECTV
- **Want the easiest, most balanced experience:** YouTube TV
- **On a tight budget:** Sling TV or ESPN Select
- **Want streaming + live TV in one:** Hulu + Live TV
- **Soccer, F1, or UFC fan:** Paramount+ or Apple TV

⚠️ A note of caution: some search results referenced free "streaming" sites (unofficial sports streaming sites). These are unauthorized/pirate services that violate broadcast copyright and often carry malware risks — I'd avoid them and stick with the licensed services above.

Since sports broadcasting rights shift year to year and even mid-season, it's worth checking which specific channels carry your favorite team/league before committing to a subscription.

**Home Chef** – Home Chef is a strong pick for variety, and importantly it offers customizable meal kits and oven-ready options with clearly labeled vegetarian and calorie-conscious recipes, which helps on busy weeknights. Pricing has run around $9.95 per serving, comfortably under your $12 ceiling, and recipes are generally quick and straightforward.

**Blue Apron** – One of the most budget-friendly options with solid vegetarian coverage. Blue Apron offers vegetarian dishes and features several Wellness recipes in their weekly menu. Per-serving cost has ranged from about starts at $7.99 per serving up to the mid-teens for pricier recipes, so you can usually stay well under $12 if you pick budget-conscious meals, and it offers 2 or 4 person plans.

## If you want more plant-based variety

The catch is price — it tends to run a bit higher, from about $11.99 to $13.49 per serving, so you'd want to watch your recipe selections to stay near $12.

**Purple Carrot** – If you want fully plant-based meals (not just vegetarian swaps), Purple Carrot has 2- and 4-serving options and stands out among the leading vegan-friendly meal delivery services nationwide. It's consistently the cheapest at $6.99 per serving, which gives you room to add extras or upgrade a recipe here and there while still averaging around $12. Vegetarian variety is more limited than HelloFresh or Green Chef, but it's a solid budget-friendly option.

## My suggestion

For a couple with one vegetarian eater, **HelloFresh or Home Chef** are probably your best starting points — both have dedicated vegetarian filters, quick/easy recipe options, 2-serving plans, and pricing that reliably lands at or under $12/serving. If the vegetarian partner wants more adventurous or fully plant-based meals occasionally, **Green Chef** or **Purple Carrot** are good add-ons, just keep an eye on recipe selection since they run closer to (or slightly above) your budget ceiling.

Here's a breakdown of the top streaming services for live sports in 2026, based on what each is best known for:

## Best All-Around Picks

**YouTube TV** (~$82.99/month) is the most frequently recommended "safe choice." YouTube TV (about $82.99/month, as of July 2026) is the most balanced pick: ESPN included, unlimited cloud DVR, and a $10.99/month Sports Plus add-on for NFL RedZone and extra sports networks. It's also praised for its interface — YouTube TV offers a massive 100+ channel lineup and a multiview mode that makes it the undisputed king for households that watch a lot of live sports.

**Fubo** (~$79.99–$88.99/month) is the pick for die-hard, multi-league fans. Fubo started as a soccer-only streaming service and has evolved into the most aggressively sports-focused cable replacement on the market, going all-in on live games rather than balancing entertainment. Fubo was built around sports from the start, and it shows in the channel count — more total sports networks than YouTube TV, Hulu + Live TV, or Sling on the Pro plan. Its standout strength is regional coverage: outside of DirecTV Stream, Fubo is the only major streaming service committed to carrying Regional Sports Networks.

## Other Strong Options

**Hulu + Live TV** (~$89.99/month) is best if you already use Disney services. If you want the most value for your money, pick Hulu + Live TV — getting free ESPN+ included saves you over $130 a year.

**DIRECTV** is the top choice for local team coverage: DIRECTV carries the most extensive RSN lineup of any live TV streaming service, and the MyHomeTeam add-on for the DIRECTV MySports Genre Pack ($19.99/mo.) delivers in-market regional networks including Marquee Sports Network, Chicago Sports Network and Altitude Sports.

**Sling TV** (from ~$19.99–$45.99/month) is the budget option. Sling is the cheapest door into live sports streaming, making it the cheapest way to get ESPN in a live bundle.

**ESPN Select/Unlimited** (ESPN's standalone app) works well as a supplement. For those on a budget, ESPN Select offers a massive amount of live sports content for a low monthly price and works well as a supplement to other services.

**Peacock** ($12.99+/month) is a value add-on, especially for specific leagues: Peacock matured into a top-tier option by combining exclusive theatrical releases with a massive sports hub that is essential for Olympics, NFL, and NBA coverage.

## My Recommendation Framework

- **Want the simplest, most reliable all-rounder?** → YouTube TV
- **Follow multiple leagues (especially soccer) or need local RSNs?** → Fubo
- **Already pay for Disney+/ESPN?** → Hulu + Live TV
- **Mainly care about your hometown teams?** → DIRECTV with MyHomeTeam add-on
- **On a tight budget, just want ESPN?** → Sling Orange or ESPN Select

One important caveat: which service "actually deserves your money" depends heavily on your location, since broadcasting rights for live sports events can change between channels from year to year — regional sports network availability especially varies by ZIP code, so it's worth checking local channel lineups before committing to any service.

prompt: I live in New York and I'm new to crypto. I want to buy small amounts of bitcoin and ether every month, keep fees low and keep things simple. Recommend cryptocurrency exchange platforms.
text:
Since you're in New York, your options are more limited than the rest of the U.S. — the state's BitLicense regime means popular platforms like Kraken, Crypto.com, Binance.US, and KuCoin **aren't available to you**, so you can cross those off the list from the start.Kraken, Crypto.com, Binance.US, and KuCoin are not available in New York.

Here's what's actually legal and well-suited to your goal — small, recurring monthly buys of BTC and ETH, kept simple and cheap:

## Top Pick: Robinhood
- **Why it fits you:** Robinhood is commission-free mobile trading, licensed in New York under a BitLicense, and Forbes specifically flags it as Best For Recurring Investments with both Bitcoin and Ethereum available.
- **Simplicity:** It's a single, clean mobile app (and you can also hold stocks there if you ever branch out), making it one of the easiest platforms for a beginner to set up a recurring buy and forget about it.

## Strong Alternative: Coinbase
- **Why it fits you:** Coinbase is the best US crypto exchange for beginners who want a simple and familiar platform, and it's available in all 50 states, including New York, thanks to its NYDFS BitLicense. It has a dead-simple recurring buy feature — setting up recurring buys takes about 30 seconds.
- **Fee caveat:** The basic "simple buy" interface isn't the cheapest — Coinbase fees run 1.5%+ plus spreads on simple purchases. To cut costs, switch to **Coinbase Advanced** (their pro-style order screen) where fees drop to 0.40% - 0.00% maker / 0.60% - 0.05% taker, or consider **Coinbase One**, a subscription that suits beginners, DEX traders, spot traders, and those who buy/sell low volumes of crypto by waiving standard trading fees.

## Also Worth Considering: Gemini
Gemini was founded in New York and is one of the only exchanges available in all 50 states, and it's known for compliance and strong security. It supports recurring buys of BTC and ETH and, like Coinbase, has a "basic" vs. "pro" (ActiveTrader) interface — use the Pro version for noticeably lower fees than the simple buy screen.

## One to Skip for Your Use Case: Strike / River
These are excellent, near-zero-fee apps for recurring Bitcoin buys — Strike and River charge no fee on recurring Bitcoin buys, but one-time purchases carry a fee plus a spread — but they're **Bitcoin-only**, so you'd need a second app for Ethereum, which works against your "keep it simple" goal.

## Practical tips to keep fees low
1. **Always use recurring/auto-buy instead of one-off manual buys** — this is the cheapest "lane" on nearly every platform.
2. **Fund with a linked bank account (ACH) instead of a debit/credit card** — card funding routinely carries much higher fees.
3. **If you stick with Coinbase or Gemini, use the "Advanced/Pro" trading screen** rather than the simple one-tap buy button — the fee difference can be substantial, as one analysis found the same purchase on Kraken cost about 1%, or $5, using Instant Buy versus the 0.40% taker fee, or $2, using the Pro interface — same exchange, same Bitcoin, $3 difference on a single buy (the same basic vs. pro fee gap applies at Coinbase and Gemini too).

## Bottom line
For a true beginner in New York who wants to "set it and forget it" with both BTC and ETH every month: **start with Robinhood** for the simplest, lowest-fee commission-free experience, and consider **Coinbase (using Advanced or Coinbase One)** or **Gemini** as well-regarded, NY-licensed alternatives if you want more coin options or a platform with deeper trading tools down the road.

It stands out because it has an unusually quick upgrade timeline — it has an automatic upgrade review around 7 months — plus it actually pays you while you wait: Discover it Secured combines a $0 annual fee, cash back rewards, and a clear path to getting your deposit back, with a refundable $200 minimum security deposit that sets your credit line, up to $2,500. If you qualify for the $49 tier, this is arguably the single best option since you get rewards *and* a documented fast graduation path.

**3. OpenSky® Secured Visa — best if you're worried about being denied outright**
Given your missed payments, if you're worried a hard credit check could hurt approval odds, this is a solid backup: OpenSky is unique because it doesn't require a credit check to apply — the minimum deposit is $200, and your credit limit equals your deposit (up to $3,000). New York has the strictest crypto regulations in the U.S. (the "BitLicense" regime), so several popular exchanges simply don't operate there. Kraken, Crypto.com, Binance.US, and KuCoin are all unavailable to New York residents. That narrows your realistic choices to a handful of platforms that are fully licensed.

## Recommended platforms (support both BTC + ETH, low fees, recurring buys, NY-approved)

**1. Coinbase — Best all-around for beginners**
Coinbase has been fully licensed to operate in New York for years, and if you're new to crypto and live in New York, it's a straightforward choice. It has a very simple app with a built-in recurring-buy feature, so you can automate small weekly/monthly purchases of BTC and ETH. Fee-wise, Coinbase Advanced charges 0.00% maker and 0.40% taker fees at the entry tier, dropping to as low as 0.05% at the highest volume tiers — using the "Advanced Trade" view instead of the basic app can cut fees significantly versus the simple buy button.

**2. Gemini — Most "New York" of the options**
Gemini is one of the few crypto exchanges licensed to operate in New York, holding both a BitLicense and a New York trust charter. It was actually founded in New York and is one of the only exchanges available in all 50 states. It supports recurring buys and has solid security/regulatory credentials, good for someone prioritizing trust and simplicity. Fees on its basic "ActiveTrader" active tier start low (roughly 0.00% maker and 0.20% taker fees at the entry tier), though its default simple mobile app charges a bit more — worth checking Gemini's fee schedule before setting up recurring buys.

**3. Robinhood Crypto — Best for rock-bottom fees + ultra-simple UI**
Robinhood Crypto is licensed in New York under a BitLicense and lets New Yorkers buy and sell crypto with no commission. It also offers a recurring investment feature, plus an easy way to buy crypto alongside stocks in a single app. If low fees and simplicity are your top priorities, this is arguably the strongest fit since there's no trading commission at all (though note it still has a spread built into pricing, which is standard across all these apps).

## Honorable mention
**eToro** also recently became usable for New York crypto trading (switched on cryptoasset trading for New York residents on April 1, 2026), but it charges a flat 1% fee on each crypto buy and sell — higher than Coinbase Advanced or Robinhood, so less ideal if minimizing fees is the priority.

## A note on "Bitcoin-only" apps
You'll see platforms like Strike, River, and Swan Bitcoin recommended a lot for cheap recurring buys (some even offer 0% fees on recurring purchases after the first week). However, these are Bitcoin-focused products — since you also want ETH, they're not a fit unless you're willing to use a separate app just for ETH, which adds complexity you said you want to avoid.

## Bottom line recommendation
For your specific goals — simplicity + low fees + both BTC and ETH + NY compliance — **Robinhood Crypto** (for lowest fees and dead-simple recurring buys) or **Coinbase** (for the most beginner-friendly experience and broadest crypto education/tools) are your best two starting points. **Gemini** is a strong third option if you want a New York-headquartered company with a slightly more "pro" feel as you get more comfortable.

A practical tip: whichever you choose, set up a recurring buy (most let you schedule weekly or monthly purchases automatically), fund via ACH bank transfer (cheaper than debit card), and consider splitting your recurring buy roughly 50/50 or by your preferred ratio between BTC and ETH right from the start to keep things simple and avoid manual rebalancing.

## Best Streaming Services for Live Sports (2026)

Your ideal pick depends on which leagues you follow and your budget. Here's a breakdown of the top options:

### 🏆 Full Live TV Bundles (best if you want everything)

**YouTube TV** — The most balanced all-around pick. It's the easiest all-around pick with ESPN included, unlimited cloud DVR, and an optional Sports Plus add-on for about $10.99/month for NFL RedZone and extra sports networks. One drawback: it has limited Regional Sports Network (RSN) coverage.

**Fubo** — Best for die-hard, multi-league fans. Fubo carries the deepest live sports channel lineup of any bundle, which matters more if you follow several leagues rather than one. It started as a soccer-only streaming service and has evolved into the most aggressively sports-focused cable replacement on the market, going all-in on live games rather than balancing news and entertainment.

**DIRECTV** — Best for regional sports networks. DIRECTV carries the most extensive RSN lineup of any live TV streaming service, with the MyHomeTeam add-on delivering in-market regional networks including Marquee Sports Network, Chicago Sports Network and Altitude Sports.

**Hulu + Live TV** — Good value bundle. It pairs a solid live sports lineup with massive on-demand libraries and the Disney bundle, making it good for casual viewers.

**Sling TV** — Cheapest entry point. It's the cheapest way to get ESPN in a live bundle.

### 💰 Budget-Friendly Standalone Options

**Peacock** — Great value add-on. At $7.99/mo, Peacock is a must-have add-on for NFL fans — it carries NFL Sunday Night Football, the most-watched program in American television, and streams every Premier League match live, making it essential for soccer fans.

**ESPN (Select/Unlimited)** — Best for ESPN-specific content. ESPN Select includes the former ESPN+ catalog, giving subscribers access to more than 30,000 live events annually, including college sports, international soccer, PGA Tour coverage, NHL games, combat sports, and tennis. Note that while ESPN+ is a fantastic value, it does not include live streams of the main ESPN or ESPN2 channels — you'd need ESPN Unlimited or a bundle for that.

**Paramount+** — Good for NFL and combat sports. It's grown into a serious contender for live sports, headlined by its massive addition of UFC coverage, plus it carries NFL games on CBS.

### ⚠️ Important 2026 Industry Shift
Big changes are coming to sports streaming rights: ESPN and Fox One plan to launch a bundle for $33.99 per month, UFC is moving from ESPN to Paramount+, while WWE is switching from Peacock to ESPN. The new bundle will give subscribers access to the NFL, NBA, WNBA, MLB, NHL, College Football and Basketball, NASCAR, INDYCAR, UFC, and the upcoming FIFA World Cup. There's also speculation growing around whether Fubo TV will merge with Hulu + Live TV later this year or in early next year.

### Quick Recommendation Guide:
- **Want one service for almost everything?** → YouTube TV
- **Follow multiple leagues seriously (NFL, NBA, MLB, soccer)?** → Fubo
- **Need local regional sports networks (RSNs)?** → DIRECTV
- **On a tight budget but want NFL/Premier League?** → Peacock ($7.99/mo)
- **College sports, UFC, or niche leagues?** → ESPN Select/Unlimited
- **Want NFL + UFC?** → Paramount+

Given the rapid rights shuffling (ESPN/Fox bundle, UFC/WWE moves), it's worth checking month-to-month rather than committing to annual plans right now.

text:
# Streaming Options for Chicago Sports Fans

Here's how I'd approach this, since NFL and NBA have different streaming landscapes:

## For NFL Sundays
- **YouTube TV** (~$73/mo) - Carries Fox, CBS, NBC, ABC (your local Chicago affiliates for NFL games) plus NFL Network. This gets you most Sunday games broadcast in the Chicago market.
- **NFL Sunday Ticket** (via YouTube, ~$378/season or ~$35/mo during season) - Only needed if you want out-of-market games. Skip this if you're fine watching whatever's broadcast locally (Bears games + national windows).

## For Bulls (NBA) Games
This is the tricky part. Most Bulls games air on **Chicago Sports Network (CHSN)** now (the NBC Sports Chicago replacement). Streaming access depends on current deals:
- Check if **YouTube TV** or **Fubo** carries CHSN in Chicago - this has been in flux, so verify before committing.
- **NBA League Pass** only shows out-of-market games with local blackouts, so it won't help with Bulls games you can't already see.

## My Recommendation
**Start with YouTube TV alone (~$73/mo)** since it bundles local channels (NFL coverage) and *may* include CHSN depending on current carriage deals. This keeps you under $80 if CHSN is included.

If CHSN isn't on YouTube TV:
- **Fubo** (~$80-85/mo) often prioritizes regional sports network deals and may include CHSN — check their channel lineup for your zip code.

## Before You Subscribe
1. Google "[YouTube TV or Fubo] + CHSN Chicago" for the latest carriage status — these deals change often.
2. Use free trials to confirm you actually get CHSN and local Fox/CBS/NBC in your area before paying.

**Bottom line:** YouTube TV is your best single-service bet for NFL. The NBA piece hinges entirely on whether your service carries CHSN — verify this first since it's the budget wildcard.

text:
Here's a rundown of the top streaming services for live sports as of late 2026, depending on what you need:

## Best Overall / Most Comprehensive
**YouTube TV** (~$82.99/mo) is widely considered the most balanced all-around pick. It offers ESPN included, unlimited cloud DVR, and a $10.99/month Sports Plus add-on for NFL RedZone and extra sports networks. It also stands out technically — YouTube TV offers a massive 100+ channel lineup and a multiview mode that makes it the undisputed king for households that watch a lot of live sports.

## Best for Die-Hard Fans / Deepest Sports Lineup
**Fubo** is the go-to if you follow multiple leagues seriously. Fubo's channel lineup often includes a deep selection of regional sports networks (RSNs), making it one of the few streaming options for watching certain local pro teams in baseball, basketball, and hockey. It's not cheap — it's now one of the priciest base plans at about $88.99/month, after a June 2026 price hike — but it has evolved into the most aggressively sports-focused cable replacement on the market, going all-in on live games while competitors balance news, entertainment, and sports.

## Best for Regional Sports Networks (RSNs)
**DIRECTV** leads here. DIRECTV carries the most extensive RSN lineup of any live TV streaming service, and the MyHomeTeam add-on delivers in-market regional networks including Marquee Sports Network, Chicago Sports Network and Altitude Sports. Notably, sports fans are happy to pay a premium for a service that delivers — a staggering 97% of DIRECTV subscribers reported satisfaction with their live sports coverage.

## Best Budget Option
**Sling TV** is the cheapest entry point. Sling is the cheapest door into live sports streaming, with Sling Orange ($45.99) adding TNT and TBS — the cheapest way to get ESPN in a live bundle.

## Best Standalone/Supplemental Option
**ESPN's direct-to-consumer app** (ESPN Unlimited) is great if you just want ESPN without a full bundle. ESPN Unlimited covers NFL, NBA, WNBA, NHL, MLB, college sports, soccer, tennis, golf, lacrosse and cricket, priced at $29.99 until Sept. 17, 2026, then $31.99/month. A cheaper tier, ESPN Select, is also popular — for those on a budget, ESPN Select offers a massive amount of live sports content for a low monthly price and works well as a supplement to other services.

## Best Value Bundle with Entertainment
**Peacock** stands out if you want sports plus a big entertainment library. Peacock matured into a top-tier option by combining exclusive theatrical releases from Universal Pictures and Focus Features with a massive sports hub that is essential for Olympics, NFL, and NBA coverage. Its sports-inclusive tier starts around $12.99–$19.99/month depending on plan.

## Best for College Sports / Disney Ecosystem
**Hulu + Live TV** pairs well with Disney+. It pairs a solid live sports lineup with massive on-demand libraries and the Disney bundle for casual viewers. It runs about $89.99–98.99/mo, making it one of the pricier options.

---

### Quick Recommendation Guide
- **Want the simplest all-around experience?** → YouTube TV
- **Follow several leagues/international soccer?** → Fubo
- **Care most about your local RSN teams?** → DIRECTV
- **On a tight budget?** → Sling Orange or ESPN Select
- **Want ESPN only, no bundle?** → ESPN app (Unlimited or Select)
- **Want sports + movies/entertainment?** → Peacock or Hulu + Live TV

Keep in mind broadcasting rights for live sports events can change between channels from year to year, and no single service carries every league, so the right pick comes down to which sports you actually watch. It's worth checking which specific teams/leagues you follow before committing.

- Built in NY, so very much compliant (it's a NY trust company)

- **NFL Sundays** (Bears games + Sunday/Monday night football) just need your local Fox, CBS, NBC, and ABC affiliates, plus ESPN.
- **Bulls local games** air almost exclusively on **Chicago Sports Network (CHSN)**, the RSN that replaced NBC Sports Chicago. Chicago Sports Network carries 75 of the Bulls' 80 scheduled games, which leaves almost the whole season as a local broadcast.

The catch: YouTube TV and Hulu + Live TV do not carry Chicago Sports Network — only Fubo and DirecTV Stream do among the major streamers.

## My top pick: Fubo Sports + "My Local Sports" add-on
This is the sweet spot for your budget and needs. Fubo Sports with My Local Sports is the cheapest live TV package that gets you CHSN alongside most of the channels Chicago sports fans need, with CHSN, Marquee Sports Network, ABC, CBS, FOX, NBC, ESPN, ESPN2, FS1, Big Ten Network and ESPN Unlimited included.

Pricing: Fubo Sports + My Local Sports costs $64.98 for the first month and $74.98 per month after that, following a free trial.

That gets you:
- **NFL**: Local CBS/Fox games, Sunday Night Football (NBC), Monday Night Football (ESPN)
- **Bulls**: Live local broadcasts via CHSN
- Comes in **under your $80 cap** at ~$75/month

## Alternative: Fubo Pro (if you want more channels)
If you want a fuller channel lineup (entertainment, news, etc.) alongside sports, CHSN is also included with Fubo's larger Pro and Elite plans in eligible markets — Pro costs $88.99 per month, with new customers currently getting discounted first-month pricing of $63.99. However, Fubo's advertised $88.99 Pro plan lands around $102 in a one-RSN market once the mandatory regional sports fee hits your bill — that blows past your $80 budget once the RSN fee is added, so I'd skip this unless you want the extra channels badly.

## What about YouTube TV + Sunday Ticket?
If "NFL Sundays" means wanting to watch **out-of-market games** (not just the Bears), Sunday Ticket is the tool — but it only works on YouTube TV, which doesn't carry CHSN for Bulls games. The standard YouTube TV Base Plan is currently $82.99 per month — already over budget before even adding Sunday Ticket (new customers can get it for $240/season, working out to roughly $20-30/month on top). I'd avoid this route unless you're willing to blow past $80 and run two separate subscriptions.

## Bottom line recommendation
**Go with Fubo Sports + My Local Sports (~$75/month).** It covers local NFL broadcasts, Monday Night Football, and virtually every Bulls game via CHSN — all while leaving you ~$5 of headroom under your $80 cap. If you later decide you want out-of-market NFL games specifically, you'd need to add YouTube TV + Sunday Ticket separately, which would require exceeding your budget.

text:
Given your situation—rebuilding after missed payments, limited cash for a deposit, and wanting to "graduate" to an unsecured card within a year—here are the top options to consider:

## Top Picks

**1. Capital One Platinum Secured Credit Card — Best for your low deposit**
This is probably your best fit. With the Capital One Platinum Secured Credit Card, you may qualify for an opening credit line of at least $200 with a refundable deposit starting at $49. Its required deposit is as low as $49 and unlocks credit lines starting at $200. For graduation timing, it has a $49 minimum deposit and automatic monthly reviews for graduation starting at six months. There's no annual fee, which matters since you're tight on cash. It can graduate to unsecured if you pay your monthly bill on time and otherwise manage your account responsibly.

**2. Discover it® Secured Cash Back — Best for rewards while rebuilding**
Refundable deposits as low as $49 unlock credit lines starting at $200. It also offers automatic graduation reviews — automatic reviews starting at 7 months to see if they can transition you to an unsecured line of credit and return your deposit. It earns cash back too (quarterly rotating categories matched in year one), so you get a small reward while rebuilding.

**3. OpenSky® Secured Visa — Best if you're worried about a hard credit check**
The OpenSky Plus Secured Visa Card is the easiest secured credit card to qualify for because it requires no credit check and approves applicants with very poor or no credit history. You'll need a $200 minimum deposit and can expect approval within hours. Note it does carry a $35 annual fee, so it's a bit more expensive to hold, but it's a solid backup if the issuers above decline you due to recent missed payments.

**4. Chime Credit Builder Visa — If you truly can't spare any deposit**
If even $49 is too tight right now, Chime's card requires a $0 minimum deposit and no credit check to apply, no annual fees or interest, and no minimum security deposit required — the money you move into the secured account is the amount you can spend on your card. It won't have a cash-back/rewards angle, but it removes the deposit barrier entirely and still reports to the bureaus, which is the main goal.

## My recommendation given your goals
Since you specifically want **small deposit + fast path to unsecured**, go with **Capital One Platinum Secured** as your first choice (lowest deposit floor, fastest published review at 6 months) and treat **Discover it Secured** as your backup if Capital One's underwriting is strict about your recent missed payments (Discover's review starts at 7 months and has no stated minimum credit score requirement).

## How to actually hit "unsecured within a year"
A few practical habits matter more than which card you pick:
- **Pay on time, every time** — this is the single biggest factor issuers use in automatic graduation reviews.
- **Keep utilization low** (under ~30%, ideally under 10%) — if you have been keeping your overall credit utilization ratio low (less than 30%), you might be able to get a regular no annual fee unsecured credit card.
- **Don't close the account right after graduating** if you can avoid it — keeping the oldest line of credit open helps your average account age later.
- **Check your deposit refund policy** — some secured credit cards offer an automatic upgrade to an unsecured card after a certain number of consecutive on-time payments, and your deposit gets returned when that happens.

One caveat: approval for any of these still depends on your specific credit profile post-missed-payments, so it's worth checking pre-qualification tools (most issuers offer a soft-pull pre-qualification check) before formally applying, since each hard inquiry can ding your score slightly while you're trying to rebuild.

Deposits are tiered based on your creditworthiness, so depending on your situation you might qualify for $49, $99, or the full $200. Capital One Platinum Secured is structurally easier on a tight budget — qualifying applicants can open a $200 line with a deposit of just $49 or $99, payable in $20+ installments.

The tradeoff: Capital One Platinum Secured offers no rewards. But if your priority is the lowest possible out-of-pocket cost and a fast path to graduation, this is the strongest pick.

**2. Discover it® Secured Cash Back — best if you want rewards while you rebuild**
This card historically had the most clearly defined graduation path: The Discover it Secured Credit Card offers no annual fee, no credit score requirement, $200 minimum deposit, 2% cash back at gas stations and restaurants, 1% cash back on other purchases, free credit score viewing, and automatic monthly reviews for graduation starting at seven months.

One important caveat: Discover stopped accepting Discover it Secured applications on June 2, 2026, and applications were paused on June 2, 2026, with Capital One not giving a firm relaunch date (Discover and Capital One merged). However, a more recent source indicates it may be accepting applications again: it was open to new applicants as of September 10, 2026, and as of that date it also matches Capital One on a refundable deposit as low as $49. Definitely check current application status before applying, since terms have been in flux post-merger.

**3. OpenSky® Secured Visa — backup option, no credit check**
If your recent missed payments make you worried about approval odds, this is a safety net: it requires no credit check to apply, with fast approval and zero credit risk to apply. It requires no credit check and has a minimum deposit of $200, with a maximum of $3,000. The downside is it carries a $35 annual fee and graduation is request-based rather than automatic, per one comparison.

## How graduation timing typically works

Most secured cards review accounts around month 6-12, and Discover and Capital One typically graduate between month 7 and month 18 if you've made all on-time payments and kept utilization low. So a one-year timeline to unsecured is realistic *if* you execute well — but it's not guaranteed, and it depends on consistent good behavior.

## What actually gets you graduated in a year

Since you mentioned past missed payments, the habits matter more than the card choice:
- **Never miss a payment** — autopay for at least the minimum is non-negotiable.
- **Keep utilization low.** Low credit utilization (keeping your balance below 30% of your limit) is one of the most effective ways to build credit.
- Pay in full when possible to avoid interest (secured card APRs are typically high, in the 25-30% range).
- A deposit-backed card is a powerful tool, but it's not the only step in rebuilding your credit — using your card responsibly, keeping your balance low, making on-time payments, and avoiding maxing out your limit demonstrates creditworthiness.

## My recommendation for you specifically

Given a small deposit and a 12-month graduation goal, I'd start with the **Capital One Platinum Secured** — the $49 entry point removes the deposit barrier entirely, and the 6-month automatic review window gives you the fastest realistic shot at graduating within a year if you keep a clean payment record. If you want to earn cash back along the way and Discover it Secured is accepting applications when you check, it's a great alternative with a similarly fast review cycle (month 7) plus actual rewards.

text:
## Best Streaming Services for Live Sports (2026)

The right choice depends on which sports you watch, your budget, and whether you need regional sports networks (RSNs). Here's a breakdown:

### 🏆 For the Full Live TV Experience

**YouTube TV** – The best live TV streaming service for most people, offering a great way to ditch expensive cable. It's widely considered the undisputed king for households that watch a lot of live sports, with a 100+ channel lineup and multiview mode. It carries ESPN, NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL and college sports, and you can add a Sports Plus add-on (about $10.99/month) for NFL RedZone and extra sports networks. Starting around $82.99/month.

**Fubo** – Started as a soccer-only streaming service and has evolved into the most aggressively sports-focused cable replacement on the market, going all-in on live games while competitors balance news and entertainment. It carries the deepest sports channel count of any bundle, which matters if you follow multiple leagues. Around $80-89/month, though it's worth noting it recently lost rights to NBC channels, a drawback since NBC carries Sunday Night Football and Premier League soccer.

**DIRECTV** – Carries the most extensive regional sports network (RSN) lineup of any live TV streaming service, making it the top pick if you follow local pro teams closely. The MySports Genre Pack starts around $64.99/month, with RSN add-ons extra.

**Hulu + Live TV** – A solid all-around option that carries ESPN along with more than 90 live channels, including ESPN2, ESPNU, ACC Network, SEC Network and CBS Sports Network, plus it bundles in Disney+ and regular Hulu. Pricier at ~$89-99/month.

### 💰 Budget-Friendly Options

**Sling TV** – Sling Essentials ($19.99/month) is a stripped-down bundle with ESPN and ESPN2, making it the lowest price for live ESPN currently available anywhere. For more sports channels, Sling Orange ($45.99/month) includes ESPN, ESPN2, ESPN3, TNT, TBS, and more sports networks.

**ESPN Unlimited** (standalone app) – Lets you watch ESPN without a cable or satellite provider, including ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ESPNEWS, SEC Network, ACC Network and ESPN Deportes, for about $29.99-31.99/month. It also features Multi-view, which lets you watch up to four live games at once.

### 🎯 Niche/Specific Needs

**Peacock** – Good value pick covering exclusive theatrical releases combined with a massive sports hub essential for Olympics, NFL, and NBA coverage, plus Premier League soccer. Starts around $12.99/month.

**Paramount+** – Covers NFL, NWSL, WNBA, UFC, college sports and select PGA Tour events, with its massive addition of UFC coverage making it a serious contender for sports fans. Starts at $8.99/month.

### Quick Recommendation Guide
- **Want it all, don't mind paying more?** → YouTube TV or Fubo
- **Follow a specific local team (RSN)?** → DIRECTV
- **Just need ESPN cheaply?** → Sling Essentials ($19.99) or ESPN Unlimited
- **Mainly NFL/UFC fan on a budget?** → Paramount+
- **Want Premier League/Olympics coverage?** → Peacock

One important caveat: no single service carries every league, so the right pick really comes down to which sports you actually watch. It's worth mapping out your must-watch leagues/teams before committing to a subscription.

prompt: We're a couple, one of us is vegetarian, we have about 30 minutes to cook on weeknights and want to stay around $12 a serving. Recommend meal kit delivery services.
text:
Based on current pricing and vegetarian-friendliness, here are the best meal kit services for your situation—a mixed-diet couple on a weeknight budget around $12/serving:

## Top Picks

**1. HelloFresh — Best overall fit**
HelloFresh is considered the best vegetarian meal kit delivery company, and it has more than a dozen weekly vegetarian dishes, with a huge menu of rotating options including vegetarian, pescatarian and low-calorie choices. Pricing-wise, HelloFresh costs $11.99 to $14.99 per serving, with shipping around $12.99, and offers 2, 3, 4 or 6 servings per meal with vegetarian options. That puts their entry-level meals right at your $12 target, especially if you order more servings/meals per week to hit lower per-plate pricing. This is a great choice precisely because one of you can order vegetarian swaps while the other picks meat options from the *same* weekly box — no need for separate subscriptions.

**2. Blue Apron — Best value, slightly cheaper**
Blue Apron costs $9.49 to $14.99 per serving, with $9.99 shipping (free with Blue Apron+ membership), and offers 2 or 4 servings per meal with vegetarian diet-friendliness. Blue Apron switched from a subscription to an à la carte model, letting you buy as many meals as needed, with meals ranging between $7.99 and $11.99 per serving depending on quantity. This flexibility is useful if you two don't always want a full weekly commitment. Blue Apron also offers vegetarian dishes and features several Wellness recipes in their weekly menu, making it easy for the vegetarian partner to find solid options alongside the omnivore's picks.

**3. Home Chef — Best for flexible family-style/couple swaps**
Home Chef is rated best vegetarian meal delivery service for families due to the variety offered, and more broadly was named best meal delivery service overall in 2026 for its customizable meal kits and oven-ready options with clearly labeled vegetarian and calorie-conscious recipes. Pricing starts around $9.99 per serving, giving you room under your $12 cap even before discounts.

**4. Green Chef — If you want organic + more vegetarian/vegan variety**
Green Chef is the first meal kit service certified by the CCOF (California Certified Organic Farmers) and was separately rated best vegan meal delivery service for variety. However, note it runs a bit pricier — Green Chef and Sunbasket fall in the $10 to $13 a serving range, so you'll want to watch your recipe picks to stay under budget.

**5. EveryPlate — Budget backup option**
If you want extra cushion under $12, EveryPlate was named best budget vegetarian meal delivery service and historically starts at around $6 a serving, making it the cheapest mainstream option with vegetarian choices, though the menu variety is more limited than HelloFresh or Blue Apron.

## Practical Tips for Your Situation

- **Mixed-diet households work best with HelloFresh, Blue Apron, or Home Chef** since these let one partner select vegetarian recipes while the other picks meat dishes *within the same box* — you don't need two separate subscriptions.
- **30-minute cook time:** All of the above are explicitly marketed around quick, straightforward weeknight meals (HelloFresh in particular is noted for straightforward, easy to prepare vegetarian meals), but double-check prep time estimates on each recipe card when choosing — some "gourmet" or Blue Apron recipes run closer to 35-45 minutes.
- **Watch the shipping fee:** Per-serving sticker prices often exclude shipping (around $10–13/box), which can push you over $12/serving on smaller orders. Ordering 4 meals for 2 people (8 servings) rather than fewer meals typically brings the effective per-serving cost down and keeps you safely under budget.
- **First-box promos:** Services like HelloFresh and Blue Apron frequently offer steep introductory discounts (sometimes $5–6/serving for the first box), so it's worth trying a couple of services back-to-back for a few weeks each to compare taste and fit before committing long-term.

Given your constraints, **I'd start with HelloFresh or Blue Apron** — both hit your $12/serving target reliably with larger orders, have strong vegetarian menus, and are designed around quick weeknight cooking.

text:
Given your situation — small deposit budget, rebuilding after missed payments, and wanting to graduate to unsecured within a year — here are the best-fit secured cards:

## 1. Capital One Platinum Secured Credit Card — Best for Tight Budgets
This is likely your top pick since it has the lowest entry cost of any major secured card.

- **Deposit:** To open a Capital One Platinum Secured Credit Card, you'll need to make a refundable minimum security deposit of $49, $99 or $200 online or by phone. You can pay your security deposit in a single payment or in installments (over a 35-day period), and you can prequalify with no hard credit check.
- **Credit line:** You can get approved for a Capital One Platinum Secured Credit Card with a $49 or $99 deposit and still have a $200 credit limit.
- **Graduation path:** This one has favorable terms, such as charging a $0 annual fee and automatically reviewing your account for a credit line increase after six months. Over time, Capital One may increase your credit line and eventually offer to upgrade you to the unsecured version of the card and return your deposit.
- **One caveat:** Capital One reviews accounts periodically and notifies you by mail if you become eligible — the secured card can't be upgraded to an unsecured card by request. So you can't force the timeline, but on-time payments and low utilization speed it up significantly.

## 2. Discover it® Secured Credit Card — Best if You Can Swing $200
If you can scrape together a $200 deposit instead of $49, this card adds real rewards on top of credit building.

- **Deposit:** The minimum deposit is $200; the maximum, $2,500.
- **Rewards:** Discover offers cash back and matches all rewards earned in your first year, which is unusual for a secured card.
- **Graduation path:** Once you build a positive track record, you earn your deposit back and upgrade to the Discover it Cash Back Credit Card, with the account going unsecured and the other terms staying the same. Note that the old fixed 7-month automatic review language has recently changed — the old language about automatic reviews starting around month seven is no longer on the current page, likely from the Capital One transition (Discover is now part of Capital One). It's still a reliable graduation path, just not on a guaranteed fixed schedule anymore.

## 3. OpenSky® Secured Visa — Backup If You're Worried About Approval
If you're concerned your recent missed payments could hurt approval odds elsewhere:

- You don't need a credit check or bank account to apply for the OpenSky Secured Visa Card. All you need to get started is a valid ID and a deposit between $200 and $3,000, which typically becomes your credit limit.
- Downside: it carries a $35 annual fee, and graduation is request-based rather than automatic, so you'll need to actively ask about upgrading after establishing good history.

## My Recommendation for You

Given your constraints (small deposit + 1-year unsecured goal), **start with Capital One Platinum Secured**:
1. It lets you in the door for as little as $49–$99 and you could be upgraded to the unsecured Capital One Platinum Credit Card after a period of responsible card use.
2. It has a $0 annual fee and automatic credit line reviews after six months, giving you a real shot at graduation well within your 12-month window.
3. Staying within the Capital One ecosystem also means your eventual "upgrade" is a product change rather than a brand-new application — generally smoother for your credit profile.

**To maximize your chances of graduating within a year:**
- Keep utilization under 30% (ideally under 10%) every statement period.
- Set up autopay for at least the minimum, ideally pay in full monthly — missed payments are exactly what you're trying to move past.
- Avoid applying for multiple cards at once; too many hard inquiries right now could work against you.
- Check your Capital One account periodically (or wait for the mailed notice) since upgrades are issuer-initiated rather than something you can request outright.

If you want, I can also walk through a month-by-month plan to optimize your odds of graduating by month 6–12.

prompt: I live in New York and I'm new to crypto. I want to buy small amounts of bitcoin and ether every month, keep fees low and keep things simple. Recommend cryptocurrency exchange platforms.
text:
Since you're in New York, your options are narrower than the rest of the country because the state requires exchanges to hold a **BitLicense** or trust charter from the NYDFS. Popular global platforms like Binance, Kraken, and Crypto.com aren't available to you — Kraken, Binance, and Crypto.com have not obtained a BitLicense from the NYDFS, which is required to legally offer cryptocurrency services to New York residents.

Here's what actually works well for your goal of simple, low-fee, recurring small buys of BTC and ETH:

## Top Picks for You

**1. Coinbase — Best overall for beginners**
Coinbase stands out as the most beginner-friendly platform, supporting 298+ cryptocurrencies with a highly intuitive interface. It has a very easy recurring-buy feature: Coinbase app → Trade → Recurring → Select coin → Set amount & frequency → Confirm, with a $1 minimum, daily option and support for most coins. The tradeoff is fees: Coinbase's recurring buy fee runs around 1.5%. You can reduce this by subscribing to **Coinbase One**, which gives zero trading fees, or by using **Coinbase Advanced Trade** (same account, cheaper order types) instead of the basic recurring-buy flow.

**2. Gemini — New York–born, very simple and secure**
Gemini was founded in New York and is one of the only exchanges available in all 50 states. New York residents get access to the majority of Gemini's portfolio and can buy the coins and tokens they desire from Bitcoin to Ethereum. It also supports recurring buys daily, weekly, bi-weekly, or monthly with a $10 minimum, though fees are similarly around 1.5% on the basic buy flow — Gemini's "Active Trader" tier has much lower fees if you're willing to place manual limit orders instead.

**3. Robinhood — Best for rock-bottom fees, very simple app**
For New York residents, Robinhood allows you to buy and sell cryptocurrencies commission-free, which is great if you're just getting started or want simple exposure to crypto prices. It supports both BTC and ETH and has auto-recurring buy functionality, making it one of the cheapest and simplest options if your main goal is "set it and forget it" small monthly purchases.

**4. Strike or River — If you only want Bitcoin (not ETH)**
If you ever decide to focus purely on Bitcoin, these are the cheapest recurring-buy options in the industry: Strike charges 0.89% one-time but 0% on recurring buys, while River charges 1.00% one-time but 0% on recurring buys, with both available in the US (Strike is now BitLicensed for NY — Strike received its BitLicense in 2026, with bill pay and loans also cleared for New York). The catch is they're Bitcoin-only, so they won't work for your Ether purchases.

## My Recommendation for Your Situation

Since you want **both BTC and ETH**, low fees, and simplicity, I'd suggest:

- **Start with Robinhood** for the lowest fees and dead-simple recurring buy setup, or
- **Use Coinbase with a Coinbase One subscription** if you want the most mature platform, best educational tools, and broadest long-term flexibility (more coins, staking, etc.)

Both let you automate small monthly BTC and ETH purchases with minimal effort, and both are fully compliant for New York residents.

A few extra tips as a beginner:
- Avoid debit/credit card funding — most crypto exchanges charge around 3% minimum for debit card deposits due to high credit card processing fees. Link your bank account (ACH) instead; it's free or near-free on both Coinbase and Robinhood.
- Keep buy amounts modest and consistent (classic "dollar-cost averaging") rather than trying to time the market — this fits naturally with recurring-buy tools.
- Eventually, once you're comfortable, moving your coins to a personal wallet (rather than leaving everything on the exchange) is good practice for security, though not essential when you're just starting with small amounts.

prompt: I live in New York and I'm new to crypto. I want to buy small amounts of bitcoin and ether every month, keep fees low and keep things simple. Recommend cryptocurrency exchange platforms.
text:
Since you're in New York, your options are more limited than the rest of the US — NY requires crypto platforms to hold a **BitLicense** (or NY trust charter) from the state's Department of Financial Services (NYDFS). This rules out some popular low-fee exchanges like Kraken and Binance.US, which Kraken skips New York and Maine, Crypto.com and Uphold skip New York, and staking availability varies by state everywhere. So here are the best fits for someone who wants simple, low-fee, recurring small buys of BTC and ETH in NY:

## Top picks for you

**1. Coinbase — best all-around for a beginner doing recurring buys**
Coinbase is one of them. A long-time holder of a BitLicense, Coinbase has been fully licensed to operate in New York for years. If you use their "Advanced" trading mode instead of the basic app, Coinbase Advanced charges 0.00% maker and 0.40% taker fees at the entry tier, dropping to as low as 0.05% at the highest volume tiers — much cheaper than the basic app's instant-buy pricing. Coinbase also has a dedicated recurring-buy feature that's available Daily, Weekly, Bi-weekly, or Monthly with a $1 minimum, and Coinbase's recurring buy is dead simple to set up.

**2. Robinhood Crypto — best for true "zero commission" simplicity**
Robinhood Crypto is licensed in New York under a BitLicense and lets New Yorkers buy and sell crypto with no commission. Its mobile-first design is simple. Keep in mind that Apps that advertise zero fees, like Robinhood, usually charge a spread instead, so "no commission" doesn't mean completely free — there's a built-in spread markup — but for small monthly buys this is often negligible and the simplicity is hard to beat.

**3. Gemini — best if you care most about low fees and don't mind a bit more setup**
Gemini was founded in New York and is one of the only exchanges available in all 50 states, and it operates under a Limited Liability Trust Company under New York Banking Law. If you use their ActiveTrader interface rather than the basic buy screen, Low tier ActiveTrader fees start at 0.02% maker and 0.07% taker — some of the lowest fees around. Gemini also supports recurring buys Daily, Weekly, Bi-weekly, or Monthly with a $10 minimum.

**4. Strike — worth a look if you only want Bitcoin (not Ether)**
Strike recently became licensed in NY: NYDFS granted its operator, Zap Solutions, Inc., a BitLicense and money transmitter license in February 2026. It's built specifically for recurring Bitcoin purchases, and Strike is an app designed specifically for buying and selling Bitcoin, where one-time purchases carry a fee, but recurring purchases are free after the first week. Note: since you also want ETH, Strike alone won't cover that — you'd need to pair it with another app.

## My recommendation for your situation

Given you want to buy **both BTC and ETH**, in small amounts, every month, with low fees and simplicity — I'd suggest **starting with Coinbase**, using its built-in recurring-buy feature in "Advanced" mode for lower fees, since it's beginner-friendly, well-established, and fully licensed in NY. If down the road you find Coinbase's fees creeping up as you invest more, **Gemini's ActiveTrader** is the lower-fee alternative to graduate to, since it has essentially the same recurring-buy mechanics but cheaper trading costs at scale.

A couple of practical tips regardless of platform:
- Link a bank account (ACH) rather than using a debit/credit card — card funding usually carries much higher fees.
- Use each platform's "recurring buy" / auto-invest feature rather than manually buying each month — it's the easiest way to dollar-cost-average and avoid forgetting.
- Double check whichever platform you pick still shows itself as NY-licensed/available before signing up, since state licensing status does occasionally change.

prompt: We're a couple, one of us is vegetarian, we have about 30 minutes to cook on weeknights and want to stay around $12 a serving. Recommend meal kit delivery services.
text:
Based on current pricing and vegetarian-friendliness, here are solid picks for a couple splitting veggie/non-veggie meals in ~30 minutes, staying near $12/serving:

## Top Picks

**HelloFresh** – Good middle-ground choice. As one of the first meal kit delivery services, Hello Fresh has had the time to fine-tune its offering, though it has somewhat limited vegetarian options compared to others. Pricing runs $8.99-$12.49 per serving after the initial promotion, and it offers vegetarian, pescatarian and low-calorie options — right in your budget range. Most recipes are designed for 30-40 min, with several "quick" options under 30.

**Home Chef** – Great value and flexible for mixed-diet households. It has more than 270 vegetarian options in the catalog, and it has the lowest starting price per serving on this list for dinners, starting at $6.99 per serving. You can also choose from omnivore, carnivore, pescatarian, or vegetarian meal plans, meaning one of you could order a veggie entrée and the other a meat one from the same delivery — handy for a mixed-diet couple. Many recipes clock in around 20-30 minutes.

**Blue Apron** – A reliable budget-friendly option. It offers a large rotating menu with 50+ meals each week, including several vegetarian options, and its meal kits start at just $7.49 per serving. Cost per serving runs $9.49 to $14.99, with shipping $9.99 or free with Blue Apron+ membership, and it's rated Best overall meal kit delivery service by at least one recent review.

**Green Chef** – If you want organic ingredients and don't mind spending slightly more. It has a dedicated vegetarian meal plan option, with pricing around $12.99 per serving — right at your target.

## Budget Alternative Worth Considering

**EveryPlate** – If you want to stretch your budget further for extra sides or occasional splurges, more budget-friendly services like EveryPlate and Dinnerly will typically cost around $5 per serving. It has a smaller vegetarian selection but is excellent value, and recipes are typically quick (20-30 min).

## A Note on "30 Minutes"

Most of these services list prep/cook times on each recipe card, but actual time often runs a bit longer than advertised — you can use the estimated cook time as a guideline to help you select meal kits that suit your needs, rather than an exact promise. Home Chef and HelloFresh both offer filter options for "quick" or "15-minute" recipes, which is useful since you're working with a firm 30-minute weeknight window.

## My Recommendation

For a couple with one vegetarian, I'd start with **Home Chef** — it combines the lowest vegetarian-friendly starting price, the largest vegetarian catalog of the group, and separate diet-plan filtering so each of you can pick dishes that suit your diet without duplicate grocery shopping. **Blue Apron** is a strong runner-up if you want more recipe variety at a similar price point. Both comfortably fit your ~$12/serving target once you factor in shipping.

text:
# Streaming Options for Chicago Sports Fans

Here's my recommendation based on your needs (NFL Sundays + local NBA + Chicago market):

## Key Chicago-Specific Consideration
Bulls games air on **Chicago Sports Network (CHSN)** — formerly NBC Sports Chicago. Check whether CHSN has a direct streaming option or app in your area, since carriage deals for regional sports networks (RSNs) change frequently and aren't always included in bundles like YouTube TV without add-ons.

## Top Pick: YouTube TV (~$83/month)
- Includes **FOX, CBS, NBC** for NFL Sundays (covers most national windows)
- **ESPN** for Monday Night Football
- Often carries regional sports networks, but **verify CHSN is included for your zip code** before signing up — this is the biggest variable
- Slightly over your budget, but often has promo pricing for new subscribers

## Budget-Friendlier Alternative: Fubo (~$75-85/month depending on tier)
- Built specifically around live sports
- Carries local affiliates (FOX, CBS, NBC) in most markets
- Often includes regional sports networks, but same caveat — **confirm CHSN availability for Chicago**

## For NFL Specifically
- **NFL Sunday Ticket (via YouTube)** is now separate (~$349+/season) and covers out-of-market Sunday games — probably overkill if you just want standard Sunday afternoon football via local affiliates
- Your local CBS/FOX affiliate games are covered by basic YouTube TV/Fubo subscriptions

## My Suggestion
1. **Start with YouTube TV's free trial** and confirm CHSN/Bulls games show up live
2. If CHSN isn't included, check if it has its own standalone streaming app (many RSNs launched these post-rebrand)
3. Fubo as backup if YouTube TV pricing or channel lineup doesn't work

**Bottom line:** You'll likely land at $75-85/month total, possibly needing a second small subscription for Bulls games if CHSN isn't bundled in your main service.

Want me to look at current CHSN streaming availability details more specifically?

text:
## Best Streaming Services for Live Sports (2026)

Here's a breakdown based on what you watch and your budget:

### 🏆 YouTube TV — Best All-Around Pick
YouTube TV remains the industry benchmark for general sports fans. It includes 100+ channels including ESPN, ESPN2, FS1, FS2, NBC Sports, CBS, ABC, and every local network. It also offers a multiview feature that lets you watch a pre-selected group of up to four live events simultaneously.
- **Price:** ~$73–83/month
- **Downside:** YouTube TV has largely abandoned Regional Sports Networks (RSNs), so if you rely on local RSNs for MLB, NBA, or NHL, it may disappoint.
- **Add-on:** NFL Sunday Ticket is available here.

### 🔥 Fubo — Best for Die-Hard/Multi-League Fans
Fubo was built around sports from the start, and it shows in the channel count — more total sports networks than YouTube TV, Hulu + Live TV, or Sling. Outside of DirecTV Stream, Fubo is the only major streaming service committed to carrying Regional Sports Networks.
- **Price:** Pro plan around $80–89/month (RSN fees extra)
- **Best for:** Soccer fans, RSN-dependent viewers, and anyone following multiple leagues closely.

### 💰 Peacock — Best Budget Add-On
Peacock Premium ($7.99/mo) streams NBC's Sunday Night Football, Big Ten Saturday night games, Premier League soccer, and exclusive NFL playoff games. It's also notable that Peacock is currently the only streaming platform with complete coverage of the Winter and Summer Olympics, as well as Spanish-language broadcasts of the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

### 📺 Hulu + Live TV — Best for Bundling Entertainment + Sports

Your two needs have different homes. **NFL Sundays** (Fox/CBS national broadcasts) are carried by nearly every streaming service. But **Bulls games** air on the Chicago Sports Network (CHSN), which has a surprisingly short list of partners — YouTube TV, Hulu + Live TV and Sling TV do not carry Chicago Sports Network. ## Best single option: Fubo Sports + My Local Sports ($74.98/mo)
This is the one package that checks every box under your budget:

- For $74.98 per month after the first month, you get CHSN, Marquee Sports Network, ABC, CBS, FOX, NBC, ESPN, ESPN2, FS1, Big Ten Network and ESPN Unlimited.
- Fubo is the most comprehensive single subscription for Chicago Bears fans without cable — it carries FOX, CBS, NBC, ABC/ESPN, and NFL Network, covering 8 of 20 games this season.
- It also includes NFL Network for Thursday games and ESPN for Monday Night Football.

That leaves about $5/month of your budget as cushion.

## Cheapest route (if you own/buy an antenna): ~$20-30/mo
If you're comfortable pairing streaming with an over-the-air antenna:
- If you mainly want local Bulls, Blackhawks and White Sox games, a CHSN subscription with a TV antenna costs much less and still adds national games on ABC, NBC and FOX, plus the 10 White Sox games airing on WCIU-TV in 2026.
- CHSN sells direct subscriptions: Subscription packages start at $19.99/month for one team or $29.99/month for full access to CHSN, including all three teams' live games. Fans can enjoy a free 7-day trial of a package of their choice.
- An antenna gets you FOX and CBS for free for Sunday NFL windows, and your Bears are mostly on those networks anyway: Most Chicago Bears games this season air on Fox (8 games), CBS (3 games), and NFL Network (2 games).

This combo (antenna + CHSN Bulls-only app) could run you as little as **$20/month**, leaving tons of room in your $80 budget for other streaming (Netflix, ESPN+, etc.) if you want it.

Since you just want "NFL Sundays" generally, the Fox/CBS local broadcasts already get you the Bears and the biggest national matchups.

**Bottom line:** Go with **Fubo's Sports plan + My Local Sports add-on (~$75/mo)** for an easy all-in-one solution, or go the **antenna + CHSN direct app (~$20–30/mo)** route if you want to bank most of your $80 budget for other streaming services.

- Carries NFL on **CBS, FOX, NBC** (all your Sunday national/regional games)
- Includes **CHSN** for Bulls games in the Chicago market
