## Budget-Friendly Alternative
If you want to stay strictly under $80:

- **FOX, CBS, NBC** are free with an **antenna** (get a $20-30 HD antenna) — this covers most NFL Sunday windows since those are broadcast games
- Pair with a **cheaper streaming service** like **Sling TV (Orange + Blue, ~$55-60/month)** for ESPN, NFL Network, and some cable channels
- Check if CHSN has its **own standalone streaming app/subscription** (they launched one separately from cable bundles — pricing has been in the $20/month range). This could get Bulls games without needing a full cable-replacement service.

## My Practical Recommendation
1. Get an antenna for free NFL broadcast games (CBS/FOX/NBC)
2. Subscribe directly to **CHSN's app** if available standalone for Bulls games
3. Add **NFL+** (~$7-15/month) for additional NFL content if needed

This combo likely lands you **under $80** while covering both priorities, though you'll juggle 2-3 apps instead of one bundle.

---

⚠️ **Caveat:** RSN streaming availability changes constantly and varies by market/deal status. I'd recommend checking **CHSN's website directly** and **YouTube TV's channel lookup tool** (enter your zip code) right before signing up to confirm current Bulls game coverage — this is a fast-moving space.

prompt: I live in New York and I'm new to crypto. I want to buy small amounts of bitcoin and ether every month, keep fees low and keep things simple. Recommend cryptocurrency exchange platforms.
text:
Good news: New York actually works in your favor here, because the state's strict BitLicense/trust‑charter requirement has already filtered the field down to a handful of well‑regulated, beginner‑friendly platforms. Several popular exchanges (Kraken, Crypto.com, Binance.US in some cases, OKX) simply don't operate in NY, so you can skip researching them entirely.

## Exchanges that are actually usable in New York

An October 2026 count of the NYDFS register found 39 licensed entities, comprising 26 BitLicense holders and 13 limited purpose trust companies, but only a few of those are consumer exchanges you'd actually want to use. Here are the best fits for your "small, recurring BTC + ETH buys, low fees, simple" goal:

### 1. Coinbase — best all-around pick for beginners
Coinbase has been fully licensed to operate in New York for years, and Coinbase New York users benefit from full compliance with NYDFS regulations, meaning tighter consumer protections and transparent operating standards. Unlike some platforms that offer a limited version of their services in New York, Coinbase offers its full suite of trading features, including wallet transfers, recurring buys, and tax documentation.

For fees, the simple "Coinbase" app has a spread-plus-fee structure, but if you switch to **Coinbase Advanced Trade** (same account, different tab), fees drop a lot: Coinbase Advanced charges 0.00% maker and 0.40% taker fees at the entry tier, dropping to as low as 0.05% at the highest volume tiers. Bonus: New York residents have had approval to stake ETH since October 2025, so later on you could even earn yield on your ETH.

### 2. Gemini — New York-born, very compliance-focused
Gemini is one of the few crypto exchanges licensed to operate in New York, holding both a BitLicense and a New York trust charter. Gemini was founded in New York and is one of the only exchanges available in all 50 states. If you want low-fee recurring buys and don't mind a slightly more "pro" interface, its ActiveTrader tier is worth a look — low tier ActiveTrader fees start at 0.02% maker and 0.07% taker. The basic/simple buy interface costs more, so switch to ActiveTrader once you're comfortable.

### 3. Robinhood — simplest, commission-free option
Robinhood Crypto is licensed in New York under a BitLicense and lets New Yorkers buy and sell crypto with no commission, with a mobile-first design that's simple. This is arguably the easiest on-ramp if "simple" is your top priority — costs are built into the spread rather than a visible trading fee, so there's nothing to configure.

### 4. Bitstamp — good if you want lower order-book fees
Bitstamp, founded in 2011, is one of the longest-running crypto exchanges and among the first to receive a New York BitLicense, with maker/taker fees starting at 0.30%/0.40%, available in all US states including New York. It's a solid, no-frills option, though its recurring-buy feature set is less built-out for casual users than Coinbase's.

## What to skip
- **Kraken** — not available in New York and Texas.
- **Crypto.com** — does not currently operate in New York.
- **Binance / OKX / Bybit** — Binance is not available in New York; the exchange does not possess a BitLicense... without this regulatory approval from NYDFS, Binance cannot legally serve New York residents. The same licensing gap keeps OKX and Bybit out as well.
- **Strike / River** — great for zero-fee recurring Bitcoin buys Strike and River charge no fee on recurring Bitcoin buys, but one-time purchases carry a fee plus a spread — but they're Bitcoin-only, so they won't cover your Ether purchases.

## My recommendation for your specific goal
Since you want **both BTC and ETH**, low fees, recurring, and simplicity as a beginner:

1. **Start with Coinbase.** Set up a recurring buy (weekly or monthly) for BTC and ETH in the simple app, then once you're comfortable, move future buys to **Coinbase Advanced Trade** to cut your fees down to near 0%/0.40% instead of the higher simple-buy spread.
2. **Gemini** is a strong backup/alternative if you want a New York-chartered trust company specifically, with similarly low fees once you use ActiveTrader.
3. **Robinhood** is the "set it and forget it" choice if you truly want zero decisions to make — no separate fee screen, no tiers, just buy BTC/ETH on a schedule.

A practical approach: open a Coinbase account, verify identity, link your bank account (ACH, not debit card, to avoid extra fees), and set up automatic recurring buys split between BTC and ETH in whatever small dollar amount you're comfortable with monthly.

prompt: I live in New York and I'm new to crypto. I want to buy small amounts of bitcoin and ether every month, keep fees low and keep things simple. Recommend cryptocurrency exchange platforms.
text:
Since you're in New York, your options are more limited than elsewhere in the U.S. because the state's NYDFS requires platforms to hold a **BitLicense** (or equivalent trust charter) to legally serve residents. Binance has not obtained a BitLicense or equivalent NYDFS approval, so residents of New York cannot legally open accounts there, and Binance.US explicitly lists New York under its unsupported states. Kraken, Crypto.com and Uphold also lack a BitLicense or trust charter and don't accept NY residents — Kraken excludes New York and Maine, while Crypto.com excludes New York alone.

Given your goals — small, recurring monthly buys of just BTC and ETH, low fees, simplicity — here are the best fits:

## 1. Coinbase (Best overall, most beginner-friendly)
Coinbase is the best US crypto exchange for beginners who want a simple and familiar platform, and it's the only major exchange available in all 50 states, including New York, thanks to its NYDFS BitLicense secured back in 2017. It supports easy recurring buys you can automate monthly. The downside: standard fees aren't the cheapest — Coinbase charges a 0.84% trading fee plus a 1% spread for beginner trading, though a Coinbase One subscription can reduce this if you trade often enough to justify the monthly cost.

## 2. Gemini (NY-based, strong security/trust)
Gemini leads the pack with both BitLicense and Trust Charter approvals, offering comprehensive services to New York residents, and it runs as a New York-chartered trust company and hasn't reported a single major hack in eight years of operation — a nice peace-of-mind factor for a beginner. It supports easy recurring purchases of BTC and ETH. Fees run 0.0%–3.49% depending on payment method and platform, so pay via linked bank/ACH rather than card to keep costs down.

## 3. Robinhood (Lowest fees for simple recurring buys)
New York residents can buy crypto through Robinhood, which has a valid BitLicense. Robinhood offers a recurring investment feature plus an easy way to buy crypto alongside stocks in a single app, and testing found it the best crypto exchange for recurring investments. Fees are notably low — Robinhood offers some of the lowest fees for Bitcoin & crypto buying at just 0.55%, and stands out by offering 0% fees on debit card deposits. If keeping fees minimal on small monthly buys is your top priority, this is likely your best bet, though its wallet/custody features are more limited than Coinbase or Gemini.

## A newer alternative: eToro
eToro switched on cryptoasset trading for New York residents on April 1, 2026, more than three years after it became the first firm to receive a BitLicense from NYDFS following the FTX collapse. It's a solid, simple option too, though it's less battle-tested for NY users than Coinbase/Gemini.

### What I'd actually suggest for your situation
Since you want **both BTC and ETH** on a simple recurring schedule with minimal fuss:

- **Pick Coinbase or Gemini** if you value a wallet you can actually withdraw crypto from, strong brand trust, and a very polished "set it and forget it" recurring-buy feature.
- **Pick Robinhood** if minimizing fees on small monthly purchases is your #1 priority and you're fine treating it more like an investment account than a crypto wallet (limited ability to move coins off-platform).

One note: Bitcoin-only apps like **Strike** and **River** have excellent (often 0%) fees on recurring buys, but Strike is an app designed specifically for buying and selling Bitcoin, with recurring purchases free after the first week — since you also want Ether, these wouldn't cover your full plan unless you paired them with a second app just for ETH, which adds complexity you're trying to avoid.

For someone new to crypto wanting simplicity above all, **Coinbase** is probably the easiest starting point, with **Robinhood** as the lower-fee alternative once you're comfortable with the basics.

text:
Here are solid picks that fit your criteria—two servings per meal, vegetarian-friendly, quick-cooking recipes, and a budget around $12/serving:

### Top Picks

**HelloFresh** – One of the most popular options and a great fit for mixed-diet households. Price per serving runs $8.99-$12.49 after initial promotion, with vegetarian, pescatarian and low-calorie options. It also has a dedicated quick-cooking line: the service offers enough variety to cater to dietary preferences like avoiding beef/pork/seafood, vegetarian, or even meals geared toward appealing to kids.

**Home Chef** – Great value and very vegetarian-forward. It has more than 270 vegetarian options in the catalog, and it doesn't hurt that it has the lowest starting price per serving on this list for dinners, starting at $6.99 per serving. It also explicitly offers quick options: Home Chef's meal kits start at a very reasonable $8.99 per serving and include various options, such as meal kits, 15-minute meal kits, oven-ready meal kits, grill-ready meal kits. Home Chef also lets you mix diet types per box, so one of you can order a vegetarian recipe and the other a meat dish in the same delivery.

**Blue Apron** – A reliable budget-friendly choice with a long vegetarian track record. It offers a large rotating menu with 50+ meals each week, including several vegetarian options, and its meal kits start at just $7.49 per serving. Pricing can range from $7.49-$15.49 per serving, so stick to the standard (non-premium) recipes to stay near your $12 target.

**Marley Spoon** – Known for flavor variety and solid vegetarian selection. Price runs $8.99-$12.99 per serving, with 20+ vegetarian options available weekly, and typical cook times are 20-40 minutes, so just filter for the quicker recipes.

**Green Chef** – If you want organic ingredients and don't mind paying slightly more. Green Chef offers recipes rather than prepared meals, but all come with pre-measured ingredients that can be prepared in 30 minutes or less, with pricing at $12.99 per serving — right at your budget ceiling.

### Budget Backup

**EveryPlate** – If you want extra cushion under $12/serving, EveryPlate is a bit more affordable than many meal services, with meals starting at $4.99 per serving because it uses less packaging and simple ingredients. Vegetarian selection is smaller than HelloFresh or Home Chef, but it's a good way to stretch the budget if you add extras like dessert boxes or snacks.

### How to Choose Between Them

- **Best overall balance for a couple (one veg):** HelloFresh or Home Chef — both let you pick a vegetarian recipe and a non-veg recipe in the same weekly box, both have strong "30-minutes-or-less" filters, and both land comfortably under $12/serving on standard plans.
- **Best for variety/flavor:** Marley Spoon, if you're willing to spend closer to $13 on some weeks.
- **Best for organic/health-conscious:** Green Chef, though it runs right at the edge of your budget.
- **Best for stretching budget further:** EveryPlate, with the tradeoff of fewer vegetarian recipes to choose from each week.

One practical tip: all of these services charge a flat shipping fee ($9.99–$12.99 typically) on top of per-serving pricing, so for a 2-person, 2-3-meal week, factor that in — it can push your effective per-serving cost up by $1–$2 unless you qualify for free shipping thresholds.

# Crypto Exchanges for Beginners in New York

Good news: New York has stricter crypto regulations (the "BitLicense"), so your options are a bit narrower than the rest of the US, but the exchanges that do operate here are generally well-established and reliable.

## Top Recommendations

**Coinbase**
- Fully licensed in NY, very beginner-friendly interface
- Has a recurring buy feature (set it and forget it monthly)
- Downside: standard trading fees can be high if you use the basic buy/sell flow
- Tip: Use "Coinbase Advanced Trade" (sometimes called Pro-style) within the same account—fees are significantly lower than the simple buy button

**Kraken**
- Available in NY, strong reputation for security
- Lower fees than Coinbase's simple interface
- Clean recurring buy feature for DCA (dollar-cost averaging)
- Slightly less "hand-holdy" but still beginner-manageable

**Gemini**
- Founded by the Winklevoss twins, NY-based company, very compliance-focused
- Has an "ActiveTrader" mode for lower fees vs. the simple app
- Offers recurring buys

## Practical Tips to Keep Fees Low

1. **Avoid the "simple/easy" buy button** on any of these apps — that's where they hide markup (often 1-2%+). Look for "Pro" or "Advanced" trading views, which usually charge a fraction of that.
2. **Set up recurring buys** (weekly or monthly) directly within the exchange rather than manually buying each time — reduces temptation to time the market and simplifies taxes.
3. **Use bank transfer (ACH)** instead of debit/credit card — card purchases often carry extra fees (sometimes 3-4%).
4. **Watch for withdrawal fees** if you plan to move coins to a personal wallet — not urgent for beginners, but good to know.

## Simple Starting Plan

1. Open an account on Coinbase or Kraken (both very straightforward KYC process)
2. Link your bank account via ACH
3. Set up an automatic recurring buy — e.g., $50 split between BTC and ETH every month
4. Use the "Advanced" trading interface if available, even for recurring buys, to minimize fees

Great question — and good instinct to think about fees and simplicity up front, since New York has some of the strictest crypto rules in the country (the NYDFS "BitLicense"), which knocks out several popular platforms.

## The New York Catch First

Before picking a platform, know that cryptocurrency trading is legal in New York, but exchanges must comply with strict New York Department of Financial Services (NYDFS) regulations and obtain a BitLicense. This means some well-known exchanges simply aren't usable from NY: Kraken excludes New York and Maine, while Crypto.com excludes New York alone, and Binance, once the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange by volume, explicitly prohibits New York residents from accessing its services.

## Platforms That Actually Work for You (NY-Licensed, Beginner-Friendly)

**1. Coinbase — Best all-around pick for beginners**
Coinbase is the best US crypto exchange for beginners who want a simple and familiar platform. It's the only major exchange on this list available in all 50 states, including New York, thanks to its NYDFS BitLicense secured back in 2017. It has a clean recurring-buy feature that lets you auto-purchase BTC and ETH monthly. The simple "Buy" tab runs ~1% spread + transaction fee, which is a bit high for small amounts — but once comfortable, switching to **Coinbase Advanced** inside the same app drops fees to roughly maker 0.40%, taker 0.60%.

**2. Gemini — NY-born, security/compliance focused**
Gemini is the other major crypto exchange that works in New York. Gemini founders Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss are based in New York so they were at the forefront of crypto regulation when the Bitlicense was announced. It's one of the only exchanges available in all 50 states and offers a recurring-buy feature too. Standard app fees run around 1.5%+spread, but Gemini's **ActiveTrader** mode has much lower fees if you want to graduate to it later.

**3. Robinhood Crypto — simplest, lowest headline fee**
Robinhood Crypto is licensed in New York under a BitLicense and lets New Yorkers buy and sell crypto with no commission. It supports both BTC and ETH, has a dead-simple interface (especially if you already use it for stocks), and offers some of the lowest fees for Bitcoin & crypto buying, selling and trading at just 0.55%. It also stands out because most crypto exchanges charge around 3% minimum for debit card deposits due to high credit card processing fees, however, Robinhood stands out by offering 0% fees on debit card deposits.

**4. Bitstamp — long track record, decent fees**
Bitstamp is one of the longest-running crypto exchanges, and it holds a New York BitLicense. It's a solid, no-frills option with straightforward recurring buy tools.

## My Recommendation for Your Specific Goal

Since you want to **DCA small monthly amounts into both BTC and ETH, keep fees low, and keep it simple**, here's the practical ranking:

1. **Robinhood Crypto** — best combo of low fees + simplicity + free ACH/debit funding for small recurring buys.
2. **Coinbase** — if you want a dedicated crypto-first app with the most educational resources and liquidity; just use recurring buys via Coinbase Advanced (not the simple Buy tab) to avoid the ~1% spread tax.
3. **Gemini** — if NY-rooted brand trust and security culture matter most to you; similar fee profile to Coinbase.

One nuance: dedicated Bitcoin-only apps like **Strike** and **River** offer 0% fees on recurring buys after an initial period, which is the cheapest way to DCA into *Bitcoin specifically* — best for Bitcoin only recurring buys — but neither supports Ethereum, so you'd need a second app just for ETH, adding complexity you said you want to avoid.

**Bottom line:** For true simplicity (one app, both coins, NY-legal, low fees), go with **Robinhood** or **Coinbase**, set up automatic monthly recurring buys split between BTC and ETH, and avoid manual "instant buy" purchases where the spread eats more of your money.

While services like YouTube TV and Hulu + Live TV pack in a ton of channels, Fubo was built from the ground up with a sports-first mentality. If you want the most value for your money, pick Hulu + Live TV — getting free ESPN+ included saves you over $130 a year. It also bundles Disney+.

- **ESPN Unlimited/Select**: Covers NFL, NBA, WNBA, NHL, MLB, college sports, soccer, tennis, golf, lacrosse and cricket, starting around $29.99/month. Great if you just want ESPN without a full bundle.

| Budget-friendly ESPN access | Sling TV |

If you follow a specific local MLB/NBA/NHL team via RSNs, go with **Fubo** or **DIRECTV** instead. prompt: I just cut cable and live in Chicago. I mostly want NFL Sundays and local NBA games and would rather not pay more than $80 a month. Recommend streaming services for live sports.
text:
# Streaming Options for Chicago Sports Fans

Here's a realistic breakdown given your needs:

## For NFL Sundays
- **YouTube TV** (~$83/mo) – Gets you FOX, CBS, NBC, ESPN for Sunday games, plus NFL Network. This is slightly over budget but is the most complete option.
- **NFL+** (~$15/mo premium tier) – Streams out-of-market Sunday games to your phone/tablet, but **does NOT include local CBS/FOX broadcasts** (which cover most Bears games). Good supplement, not a full solution alone.
- **Fubo** (~$85/mo for base plan with FOX/CBS) – Similar price to YouTube TV, strong sports focus.

## For NBA (Bulls) Locally
This is the tricky part. The Bulls' local broadcasts are on **Chicago Sports Network (CHSN)** (formerly NBC Sports Chicago). Streaming access depends on current distribution deals:
- Check if **CHSN's own streaming app/subscription** is available standalone in your area (regional sports networks have been shifting to direct-to-consumer models).
- YouTube TV and Fubo both typically carry regional sports networks, so one subscription could cover both NFL Sundays and Bulls games if CHSN is included in the channel lineup for Chicago.

## My Recommendation
**Start with YouTube TV or Fubo** — check their channel lineup tool (enter your Chicago zip code) to confirm CHSN is included before subscribing. That single service likely covers ~90% of what you want:
- Local NFL (FOX/CBS/NBC) ✅
- NFL Network ✅
- Bulls games via CHSN (if included) ✅

## Budget Reality Check
Hitting exactly $80 with *everything* included is tough — expect $80-90/mo for a service that truly covers both NFL Sundays and local NBA without separate add-ons. Confirm local channel availability before committing, since RSN carriage deals change often.

**Next step:** Want me to help you figure out NFL Network/RedZone or ESPN+ needs too? That affects which tier you'd pick.
